title: Odometer
description: A number whose digits roll on individual slots like a mechanical counter, carrying from the low digits up so unchanged digits never move, with softened slot edges while rolling, dimmed decimals, a separate sign, a dashed loading state, and a tinted liquid glass delta chip that buds out from behind the figure after each change, rests joined beside it and melts back in.

contents.content: Slot-machine number with a single spring-driven `Animatable` value behind every digit. The digits are content, set semibold at whatever size you give them. After a change the delta is a tinted glass chip that buds out from behind the figure's trailing edge, rests a neck's width beside it, and melts back behind it when it goes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One `Animatable` number drives every slot. Each digit's roll is derived from that number and carries upward only while the digit below passes 9, so higher digits stay perfectly still until a carry reaches them. While a digit is between faces its slot edges soften, like a drum turning behind a window: the softening eases in as a digit leaves its face and out as it seats, so the edges sharpen with the landing. The roll runs on a spring with no bounce, so it never shows a digit the value never had, and its duration grows gently with the size of the change, up to 1.2 s; there is no per-frame loop.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A new value mid-roll merges into the turning drum instead of restarting it, and the layout keeps every slot the in-flight number still needs: a high slot that reads zero narrows to nothing along with its separator, and spare slots fold away only once the drum has stopped. Only the latest roll lands, clearing the tint and playing the settle tick, so `ticksOnSettle` gives one `.selection` tick per landing. A roll that lands behind the loading dashes clears its tint without a tick.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The layout (grouping separators, decimal separator, currency symbol) is read from the formatted target once per change. Use plain decimal or currency styles; compact notation such as `1.2K` will not match the rolled digits. Leading symbols always show, and the number never gives up width to the delta chip.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Decimals and their separator are dimmed by default. The sign is its own glyph and slides in or out at the zero crossing. After each change the delta is a liquid glass chip, tinted sage for up and red for down with ink text, that shows the signed amount for 1.6 s. It is born behind the figure's last digit, shrunk and clear, and buds out with visible give to rest a neck's width beside the number, its amount arriving just after, while the number makes room a beat behind the roll. Going away, its amount blurs off at once, its tint drains and it slides back behind the digits on a spring with no bounce, fading as it gets there, and the number closes up. A change while it is showing rolls its amount without overshoot, blurs its arrow across when the direction turns, and resizes and recolors the glass in place with a little give.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets `up` and `down` (the chip's glass tints), `ink`, `muted`, `dimsFraction`, and `tintsWhileRolling` (tints the digits from the start of a roll until it lands, switching without a fade; best on dark grounds).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isLoading` swaps every digit for a dash. When it ends, the dashes give way to digits at once and the first real value rolls up from zero.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion nothing rolls: the number lands on its new value at once, each changed digit switching in place, and with no roll there is no roll tint. The sign fades instead of sliding, and the delta chip fades in and out in place beside the number instead of budding; the dimmed decimals and the settle tick are unchanged. Under Reduce Transparency the chip's glass draws solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the final formatted value only, never the intermediate frames. Apply `.font` to the `Odometer` to set its size; the piece sets every string semibold, as the whole library does, so size alone sets the hierarchy. Slot sizes are measured from that font.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A full dashboard screen ships in SwiftPieces Pro (`dashboard-screen`).

title: Ring Breakdown
description: A composition ring of solid color blocks with rounded seams that you scrub by dragging around it, with a haptic at each slice boundary and a radial lift for the selected slice while the rest step back to the surface, around a semibold center figure under a liquid glass label pill whose name morphs letter by letter and out of which the selected slice's share buds as a tinted chip, above a legend of glass chips resting apart that take the slice's tint when picked.

contents.content: Ring chart with scrub-to-select, a lifted slice, and a built-in legend. The ring is content; its chrome is liquid glass. In the center a glass pill names the selection, morphing letter by letter, and the selected slice's share buds out of it as a chip tinted with the slice's color, resting joined to it. The legend rows are glass chips resting apart; the picked one takes its slice's tint.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Slices are solid color blocks from the house palette (red, sky, butter, sage, lilac, sand), separated by a 4 pt gap with rounded ends. Each slice is filled and stroked with a round join, so the corners stay soft at any size.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Drag anywhere on the ring and the selection follows your finger around it, with a `.selection` tick at every slice boundary. Release keeps the selection; tap the hole or the selected legend chip to clear it. Only changes made on the ring, the legend or with VoiceOver tick: a parent setting `selection`, or new data clearing it, stays silent.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The selected slice pulls 6 pt outward along its mid-angle with visible give and lifts a soft shadow, and drops back firmly when it lets go. The others step back to a solid resting color a beat later on a calmer spring, never a faded wash, so a selection reads as one wedge pulling out; clearing brings everything back together. The center is liquid glass over a semibold figure with dimmed decimals: a glass pill names the selection ("Total" when nothing is picked), morphing letter by letter, and the selected slice's share buds out of the pill's end as a chip tinted with the slice's color, resting joined to the pill by a liquid neck while the pair slides over to stay centered. Moving to another slice keeps the chip out: its share rolls and its tint changes in place. Clearing the selection drains its tint and melts it back into the pill. The figure and the share roll without overshoot. The legend is a stack of glass chips resting apart; the picked chip takes its slice's tint with ink text on the slice's beat, the other chips' text steps back on the same follow-through while their glass stays whole, and chips sink slightly when pressed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The ring sweeps in clockwise from the top on first appearance, and again only when data lands in an empty ring, while the center pill and figure are there from the start. New values after that slide the seams to their new angles with no overshoot, even when the selection changes with them, the center figure rolls to its new value, and the selection stays while its label is still there. A slice that arrives opens from the seam between its neighbors as they make room, and one that leaves folds back into it, so the ring never shows more than the whole.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `tint` overrides the first slice; `color` on a slice overrides any slice. `Style` sets `blocks`, `rest`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`, `gap`, and `cornerRadius`. The default thickness is 34 pt. Every string is semibold; size sets the hierarchy.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The ring is one VoiceOver element: it reads the selected slice or the total, and swiping up or down moves the selection. Legend chips are 44 pt buttons with their value. Reduce Motion drops the lift, the share chip's bud (it fades in and out in place beside the pill), the letter morph (the name crossfades) and the press scale (a pressed chip dims instead), fades the ring in instead of sweeping it, and crossfades digits instead of rolling them. New values still slide the seams, and slices still open and fold, on a shorter spring with no overshoot. Colors, the shadow and the haptics stay. Under Reduce Transparency the glass draws solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Labels are the identity, so keep them unique. `selection` lets a parent drive or observe the selected slice, and a selection set before the ring appears is kept. An id that names no slice draws as no selection.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A full budget screen built on a spending ring ships in SwiftPieces Pro (`spending-ring`).

title: Scrub Chart
description: A liquid glass line or bar chart: a semibold readout with dimmed decimals beside a tinted glass delta chip, a glass flag that rides the scrub rule with the range's change budding out of it and resting joined while a range is held, hold-and-drag range selection, and a range picker of joined glass segments whose tint flows into the one you pick as it swells, morphing the line between datasets.

contents.content: Time-series chart with scrubbing, range selection, and a morphing range picker. The chart is content; its chrome is liquid glass. A glass flag rides the scrub rule, and while a range is held the range's change buds out of the flag and rests joined to it. The range picker is a row of glass segments joined by liquid necks: the one you pick swells and takes the accent tint, which flows to it through the necks.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The readout is display type: an uppercase meta line (range, point time, or held span), a semibold 44 pt figure with its decimals dimmed, and a liquid glass delta chip beside it, tinted sage for up and red for down with ink text, and left clear with muted figures when nothing changed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One finger drags to scrub: a rule and a butter dot sit on the nearest point, and a glass flag grows out of the top of the rule with its time. They move with the finger on the same frame and never ease after it, so the figure, the rule, the dot and the flag always agree, and `.selection` ticks at each point reached (not on release). Touching down brings the cursor in with the dot a beat ahead; letting go clears it and the flag sinks back into the rule. Holding still for 300 ms before moving pins the point under the finger as an anchor: the dot pops with a rigid tap and the drag becomes a range, a solid band fills the span and the figure shows the signed change with its percent. The range's change also buds out of the flag's side, on the side toward the middle of the plot, as a tinted glass chip that rests joined to the flag by a liquid neck; the flag keeps the pair inside the plot, and when the range ends the chip's tint drains and it melts back into the flag.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Figures roll straight to their new value when the mode changes (touch, pin, release, range switch), never counting through the values between and never overshooting, and change at once while you scrub. The delta chip's glass around them resizes with a little give, and its arrow blurs across when the direction turns.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every series is normalized to 0...1 for drawing, so the y-scale never jumps between ranges. In `.line` mode datasets are resampled to 64 positions and switching ranges bends the line into the new one with no overshoot; the latest dot and the dashed baseline ride it, and the min and max labels leave at once and return once it lands. In `.bars` mode bars grow to their new heights and the active bar takes the accent block. New data in the same range morphs the same way without ending a scrub or a held range, and the min and max labels stay unless the min or max itself changed. When the chart goes from no data to data, on first appearance or when data loads later, the line unfolds from its baseline and bars rise from the floor, unhurried and without overshoot. A lazy list that rebuilds the row plays this again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At rest: no y-axis, one dashed baseline at the first value, monospaced min and max markers, the latest point as a butter dot, and three uppercase date labels whose format follows the span of the range. The picker is a row of glass segments, 44 pt tall, joined by liquid necks: segments press in lightly, and the one you pick swells and takes the accent tint, which flows to it through the necks with a little give while the one it leaves narrows and drains back to clear glass. A range set through `range` from outside moves it the same way.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `tint` sets the line (the house text color by default). `Style` sets `accent` (also the picked segment's glass tint), `up` and `down` (the delta chips' glass tints), `ink`, `muted`, `band`, `ground` (the card the chart sits on), and `numeralSize`. `format` takes any `FormatStyle` from `Double` to `String`; deltas reuse it with a sign. `range` lets you own the picker index. An empty series shows "No data yet".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver gets one element with the latest value and change; swipe up or down steps the scrub point, and swiping up past the latest point lets it go.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion the chart appears in place without unfolding, a range switch bends the line on a shorter spring, the picker's tint crossfades and its widths settle on a short spring with no give, the figures crossfade instead of rolling, the delta chip and the flag fade in without scaling, the range's change chip fades in beside the flag instead of budding, and a pinned anchor skips the pop but keeps its tap, band and readout change. Under Reduce Transparency the glass draws solid. Every string and symbol is semibold; size sets the hierarchy.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A full dashboard screen ships in SwiftPieces Pro (`dashboard-screen`).

title: Outcome Screen
description: A success, failure or empty outcome view sharing one choreography, where a ring draws, floods into a solid color block, the mark strokes in dark ink, one pulse lands with a haptic, and the headline and a signal-tinted liquid glass action rise. On failure an async retry morphs the action's label to "Retrying" while a progress bubble buds out of its end on a liquid neck, and a glass details block opens to the technical text.

contents.content: Success, failure or empty outcome view with one shared choreography: a ring, a solid block, an ink mark and one liquid glass action. The action is a signal-tinted glass capsule. While a retry runs, its label morphs to "Retrying" and it gives up a little of its width to a progress bubble that buds out of its trailing end and rests joined to it by a liquid neck; when the retry returns, the bubble melts back in and the capsule takes its width back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Three outcomes share one choreography, a stamp landing: a ring is drawn in ink, color pools inward from it once it closes and the ring takes the block's color (sage for `.success`, butter for `.failure`, sky for `.empty`), then the mark is pressed in. The outcome lands on one beat: its haptic, a small thud of the block and one ripple. The headline and message rise together, and the actions follow a beat behind, landing with a little give. Change the view's `.id` to replay it from the start.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Passing a new `outcome` to the same view restamps in place instead of swapping: the old mark lifts as the block recolors, the new mark is pressed in, and the new outcome lands with its own haptic. The copy and actions crossfade and reflow together, and the action's label morphs letter by letter to its new title. A view that reappears keeps its landed outcome and plays nothing again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.empty` draws an open tray and plays a light impact, for first-run and no-results states.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The headline is set large and tight at `.largeTitle`; `eyebrow` adds a small uppercase line above it. Every string is semibold, so size and color carry the hierarchy.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The primary action is a liquid glass capsule tinted with `signal` (the brand red, `#FF0000`, by default) under dark ink. It sinks a few points while pressed and springs back with a little give. `secondary` is a quiet text button.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On failure, `retry` turns the primary action into "Try again". Tapping it morphs the label to "Retrying" while a round glass bubble with a spinner buds out of the button's trailing end: born inside the end, it springs out on a liquid neck as the button gives up its width, and rests joined to it. When the work returns, the bubble melts back in on a spring with no bounce and the button takes its width back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `details` adds a glass panel, apart from the button, that opens to selectable monospaced text and closes a little quicker than it opens.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` holds the three blocks, the ink, the signal tint and its ink, the text colors and the details panel's glass tint (`raised`, clear by default), with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. `accent` still overrides the block.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Before iOS 26 the button, bubble and panel draw on a frosted material with a light rim, and the bubble sits beside the button without a neck. Under Reduce Transparency they are solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion the stamp fades in whole instead of being drawn, then lands with its haptic, and the copy and actions fade in a beat later without rising. A restamp recolors the block and swaps the mark briefly, with no thud or ripple. The label crossfades, the progress bubble fades in and out beside the button, the pressed button shifts a shade instead of sinking (darker in light mode, lighter in dark), and the details fade open.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a complete purchase screen, see the Pro Purchase screen.

title: Rating Scrub
description: A star rating you tap or scrub, with soft rounded stars that fill as solid blocks colored by the score and rise under your finger like soft keys, falling back in a ripple when you let go, with a little give past either end. While you scrub, a glass readout tinted with the score buds up out of the touched star and rides from star to star, and the caption under the stars is a glass numeral pill joined to a tinted label chip whose word morphs letter by letter.

contents.content: Tap-or-scrub star rating with lift, staggered settle, a score-colored fill, a liquid glass readout and an adjustable accessibility element. The stars are content and stay solid. The chrome is glass: while a finger scrubs, a readout bubble tinted with the score buds up out of the touched star, rides with the finger from star to star, and melts back down into the star the finger leaves. A tap alone never raises it, so a quick rating stays quiet.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Stars are soft rounded shapes that fill as solid blocks. They are the content, so they stay solid; the chrome around them is liquid glass. The block follows the score through `Style.levels` (the brand red, sand, butter, sage, sky by default), so a low rating reads differently from a high one at a glance. Pass `tint` to use one color for every score.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One `DragGesture` with zero minimum distance handles tap and scrub. The row works like soft keys: the star under the finger rises on a short spring with no overshoot, and the two stars either side of it rise a little after it, less with distance. Let go and the star you left drops first and each neighbor follows 30ms later, so the row falls back in a ripple. The lift is decoration only: the fill and numeral land on the value with no delay or overshoot, quickly under the finger and on a firm spring from VoiceOver or the binding, so a star never shows a score that isn't true.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While you scrub, a glass readout tinted with the score buds up out of the touched star: born behind it as a small round bubble, it rises above the lifted star while it widens to fit the rating and its label, then rides from star to star with your finger, changing tint and morphing its word as it goes. Let go and it narrows and sinks back into the star you left, its tint draining as it melts. A quick tap never raises it, so a single rating stays quiet.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: With `labels`, a caption sits under the stars: a glass pill with the numeral, a dimmed decimal and "/ 5", joined by a liquid neck to a glass chip tinted with the score that carries the label for the rounded-up rating. The chip morphs its width, tint and word letter by letter as the rating changes. Unrated, the chip is clear glass reading "Tap or slide".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pull past either end of the row and the end star gives a few points with rubber-band resistance, about the gap between two stars, then springs back at the speed you let go. The rating itself stays at 0 or the maximum. A scrub the system cancels, such as a scroll taking over, lets the stars and the readout go the same way.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every string is semibold, so size and color carry the hierarchy. Before iOS 26 the readout, pill and chip draw on a frosted material with a light rim, and the pill and chip sit side by side without a neck. Under Reduce Transparency they are solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: nothing rises, ripples or gives past the ends. The star under the finger shifts a shade in place instead (deeper in light mode, lighter in dark), the readout fades in and out above it at full width, the words crossfade, and the haptics and colors are unchanged.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: `.selection` on each step, a rigid impact when the value hits 0 or the maximum.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isReadOnly` removes the gesture, the readout and the VoiceOver adjustable action but keeps the value readable; its chip reads "No rating" until there is one. `size` scales with Dynamic Type.

title: Reaction Toggle
description: A liquid glass like or save toggle. It presses in, its glass capsule floods with its tint from the symbol outward while the symbol swaps to its filled form and squashes and springs like soft rubber, the count rolls, and a confirmation pill buds out of the capsule on a liquid neck and melts back into it.

contents.content: Liquid glass reaction toggle with press feel, a tint that floods the glass from the symbol, a rubbery symbol squash, and an optional rolling count and confirmation pill that buds out of the capsule.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At rest the toggle is a neutral liquid glass capsule. Turning it on leads with two things on the tap: the tint floods out of the symbol to the rim, showing through the glass as it spreads, and the symbol swaps to its filled form in dark ink, blurring from one to the other, and squashes like soft rubber, flattening wide, springing up tall with a small tilt and wobbling to rest. Two beats (140 ms) later the glass takes the tint as its own, so at rest the capsule is tinted glass rather than a flat block. The count rolls with the toggle, never behind it and never past its number. Turning it off drains the tint back into the symbol with no bounce or haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: With `confirmation`, a glass pill with a check buds out of the top of the capsule once the glass has taken the tint: born inside the capsule, shrunk, it springs out on a liquid neck that thins as it goes and rests joined to the capsule above it. 1.3 s after the tap it reaches its neck back out and melts home on a spring with no bounce, its words gone the moment it heads in, so nothing ever sits over the symbol. Turning the toggle off calls it home at once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` holds the tint (`fill`), the `ink` on it, the glass tint while off (`restFill`, clear by default), the rest ink, and the pill's glass tint (`pillFill`, clear by default) and ink, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. The default tint is the brand red, `#FF0000`. `tint` still works and overrides `fill`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Set `isContained: false` for a bare symbol that fills like a sticker under an ink outline. With no glass to flood, it keeps its halo: one ring ripples off the symbol a beat after the tap. Its pill has nothing to bud from, so it rises in on its own above the symbol.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The press comes from a `ButtonStyle`, so it tracks the real touch: it sinks about 2.5 pt per edge with no overshoot and springs back with a little give on release. It stays centered and never reads the touch point, so it is safe in scrolling feeds. The squash and the pill are visual only, so the hit area and layout never move.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `count` is the base value from your model; the view adds one while `isOn` so the number rolls immediately without a round trip. `size` scales with Dynamic Type and the hit area never drops below 44 pt. Every string and symbol is semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Before iOS 26 the capsule and pill draw on a frosted material with a light rim, and the pill joins the capsule without a neck. Under Reduce Transparency they are solid, and the tint arrives without the flood.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion the flood fades in and out at full size instead of spreading and draining, the symbol and the count crossfade, the pill fades in and out where it rests, the press shifts a shade instead of sinking (darker in light mode, lighter in dark), and there is no squash or halo. Nothing waits a beat. The soft haptic still fires on the off-to-on edge only.

title: Skeleton Loader
description: Solid placeholder bones and a self-masking modifier that turns any layout, color blocks included, into one quiet shape sweeping a soft diagonal highlight on a shared clock, then hands off as content unblurs and rises row by row. The bones stand in for content, so they stay solid rather than glass.

contents.content: Standalone placeholder bone. Use `.skeleton(isLoading:)` to redact real content instead. Bones stand in for content, not chrome, so they stay solid in the liquid glass language: glass is for the controls that load around them.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.skeleton(isLoading:)` keeps the real view in the tree, hidden, so layout never jumps. The placeholder is a silhouette of the redacted view drawn through an alpha threshold, so text bars, color blocks and symbols all become one solid bone color, whatever colors the content uses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A soft diagonal light passes over the bones, easing in and out, then rests before the next pass. Every instance reads the same reference clock, so passes start on the same beat. Bones and rows are crossed edge to edge in the first three quarters of `period`, so they are lit in the same moments whatever their width. Larger surfaces, up to a whole screen, stretch their pass toward nine tenths of `period` to keep the light calm, so it runs only a little quicker than a row's and rests less.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On handoff the placeholder lifts away first on a quick, firm fade, and 50 ms later the content surfaces behind it, unblurring and rising 6 pt on a calm spring with no visible overshoot, so the two barely overlap out of register. `staggerIndex` delays each row's handoff by 60 ms per index so lists reveal top to bottom. Turning loading back on covers every row at once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isFailed` stops the sweep and dims the bones firmly so the slot reads as empty; flip `isLoading` back on to retry, and the bones brighten as the light returns.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the bone `fill`, the sweep `highlight`, the `period` and the failed opacity, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. Pass the same style to `SkeletonLoader` bones and `.skeleton` so they match.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion the light holds still and every bone breathes slowly toward the highlight and back in unison, over two periods, so the slot still reads as loading. The handoff is a short crossfade with no blur, rise or stagger, so the slot never flashes empty.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Transparency switches to an opaque fill without the sweep or the breath.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Bones stand in for content, not chrome, so they stay solid rather than liquid glass: glass is for the controls that load around them. The example rows are semibold throughout, like every string in the library.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a whole projects screen that starts as ghost rows and hands off to real content, see the Pro Projects screen.

title: Status Morph
description: One continuous stroke that spins as a loading arc, closes into a ring, floods into a solid block and draws a check in dark ink on success, or a cross with a nudge on failure, with an optional caption on a liquid glass pill under the ring whose label morphs letter by letter.

contents.content: Idle, loading, success, and failure in one ring that lands as a solid block, with an optional caption on a glass pill.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Loading is a 72% arc in ink turned by a `TimelineView` clock, so nothing runs while idle or settled. Each spin starts from rest wherever the stroke lies and reaches full speed within about half a second.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On success or failure the arc keeps its angle and coasts to rest at the speed it was turning, never swinging back, while it closes into a ring. A beat later the ring floods inward into a solid block (sage for success, the brand red for failure), and a beat after that the check or cross draws in dark ink. The stroke and the block are the content, so they stay solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The outcome lands as the block closes solid, about half a second after the change, while the mark finishes drawing: success plays the `.success` haptic and, with `pops`, a soft pop; failure plays the `.error` haptic and a short shake sized to the ring, on the same beat.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `captions` puts the caption on a liquid glass pill just under the ring. A changed caption morphs letter by letter: letters the two words share hold still and the rest blur through, so "Saving" becomes "Saved" in place, and the pill eases to its new width. An outcome's word changes two beats after the state, so it lands with the mark it names. With nothing to bud from, a caption that appears rises in on its own and one that goes sinks away; the slot keeps its height, so the ring never moves. The caption is quiet while working and full ink once settled, all in semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Retrying from a settled state runs the morph in reverse: the mark un-draws, the arc turns back to ink and opens as it starts to turn, and the block drains outward into it in its own color. Going straight from success to failure recolors the ring, then the block a beat later, and swaps the check for the cross. Draining, the marks show only through what is left of the block, so ink never shows over the open center. Drawing in, they see the whole block, so the cross's first stroke never breaks as it crosses the closing center.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each mark thins to nothing over the first few percent of its stroke, like a pen landing and lifting, so an un-drawn check never leaves its round cap behind.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A change that arrives mid-morph retargets from wherever the ring is, and a landing from an earlier state never plays late. An outcome left for idle before it lands still plays its haptic at once, without the pop or shake. A retry or the other outcome replaces one that hasn't landed, so only the newer outcome is felt. If the haptic matters, keep the view on screen until the outcome lands, for example before dismissing a sheet on success.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` holds the two blocks, the ink, the arc and track colors and the caption colors, with house palette defaults that adapt to light and dark. `tint` still works and overrides the success block.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The check and cross are one `Shape` stroked to a progress, so the cross draws its two lines in order.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A view that appears already settled shows its final block and caption without replaying the morph or its haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `size` is a `@ScaledMetric`, so the ring grows with Dynamic Type alongside its caption.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Before iOS 26 the caption pill draws on a frosted material with a light rim; under Reduce Transparency it is solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion the arc does not turn: while loading it holds still and breathes slowly in opacity, so it still reads as work in progress without a caption. Each change lands in one short beat with no rotation, pop or shake, and the mark shows through the block as it fills. The color, the mark, a crossfaded caption and the haptics still carry the outcome.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full agent task screen with a live tool timeline, see the Pro Agent Task screen.

title: Glass Action Menu
description: A liquid glass action menu. Hold the signal trigger and its actions bud out of it along a line or an arc, each born inside it and pulling a neck that thins and snaps, with its name budding from its side; slide across them and release to fire. The others melt home first and the fired one last, as the trigger lands a check; a tap toggles and a scrim dismisses.

contents.content: Floating liquid glass action menu with a hold-slide-release gesture, a dimming scrim and a confirming trigger. The trigger and its actions are glass bubbles in one liquid group. The actions rest apart, from the trigger and from each other. Opening, each one buds out of the trigger: born inside it, it pulls a liquid neck that thins and snaps as it springs to its place, and its name buds from its side and stays joined to it by a neck. Closing, the names melt into their actions and the actions melt home, farthest first; after a fire the chosen action melts home last.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Two ways in: a tap toggles the menu, a 350ms hold expands it and keeps the same touch live, so you can slide across items (each crossing lifts the item and ticks `.selection`) and release to fire. Releasing a hold on empty space leaves the menu open. A touch the system cancels lets go without firing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Liquid glass throughout: the trigger, the actions and their names are glass shapes in one liquid group (`GlassEffectContainer` on iOS 26). The actions rest apart, 26pt from the trigger and from each other, so each is its own bubble; a name rests joined to its action, 6pt off its side, so a liquid neck holds them together.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The trigger leads: it sinks under the finger without bouncing, springs back on release and turns to a close mark on a crisp snap. The actions then bud out of it, 50ms apart: each is born inside the trigger, shrunk, and springs out to its place on the split spring, pulling a neck that thins and snaps as it goes. Each name buds from its own action 160ms later, squeezed narrow inside the action and stretching out to full width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Closing: the names melt into their actions first, then the actions melt home, farthest first, 40ms apart, on a spring with no bounce, so none pokes out through the far side of the trigger. A bubble's icon or name blurs away the moment it heads home, and a tinted action drains to clear glass as it melts in, so nothing sits on top of the trigger's symbol.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A hovered item lifts with a little elastic give and leans a few points toward the finger on its tether. The lean is visual only; hits always use the items' resting positions.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Firing: the rigid haptic lands on release, the item swells, and its action runs 140ms later. The other actions melt home first and the chosen one melts in last, still swollen; the trigger's close mark blurs into a checkmark as it arrives and holds it for 0.9s (`Style.confirmsAction`). No second haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The scrim is an oversized background behind the trigger; it dims everything beneath the menu in its parent and dismisses on tap. It fades with the menu and lets taps through as soon as the menu starts to close. Place the menu last in a `ZStack` so nothing sits above it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Phases: `collapsed`, `expanding`, `open`, `hovering`, `firing`, `collapsing`. Reduce Motion fades the actions and names in and out at their places with no stagger or neck, rings the hovered item instead of lifting and leaning it, shades the trigger on press instead of sinking it (darker in light mode, lighter in dark), and swaps the open trigger's symbol for a close mark instead of turning it. Haptics and the checkmark stay. Reduce Transparency draws every bubble as an opaque fill.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver sees the trigger as a button (double tap toggles) and each item as its own button while the menu is open.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Items take an optional `tint` (`Item(symbol:label:tint:action:)`): tinted glass with dark ink, for an action that needs to say something. Untinted items are neutral glass with ink that follows the appearance.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The trigger is signal-tinted glass with the house ink by default (`tint` is optional; `nil` uses `Style.trigger`). All type and symbols are semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style`: `trigger`, `ink`, `labelInk`, `triggerSize`, `itemSize`, `scrimOpacity`, `confirmsAction`; `labelFill` is kept for existing code but no longer used, since names are neutral glass. In an arc of three or more, the top item's name sits above it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Before iOS 26 the same choreography runs on a frosted fallback, where shapes don't merge into a neck.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a floating pill that morphs into a full toolbar and panel, see the Pro Reader screen (`morph-nav`).

title: Glass Mode Bar
description: One liquid glass body that turns into whatever mode you pick. At rest a capsule of mode icons spans the width; tap one and a signal anchor carrying that mode buds out of the capsule's leading end while the capsule draws back to make room and trades its icons for that mode's own controls, a waveform for voice, thumbnails for photos, chips for a timer. Tap the anchor and it melts home as the icons come back. The body keeps its footprint the whole time.

contents.content: One liquid glass body that becomes the controls of the mode you pick, without leaving its place. At rest a capsule spans the width offered, its mode icons spread evenly across it. Tapping a mode buds a signal anchor out of the capsule's leading end, carrying that mode's icon, while the capsule draws its leading edge back to make room and trades its icons for the mode's controls, which you build. The two rest joined, one body. Tapping the anchor melts it home into the capsule as the icons return. The outer edges never move. `swift @State private var mode: String? GlassModeBar(modes: [ .init(id: "voice", systemImage: "mic", title: "Voice"), .init(id: "timer", systemImage: "timer", title: "Timer"), ], selection: $mode) { mode in switch mode.id { case "voice": RecordingControls() default: TimerChips() } } `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One body that keeps its footprint. At rest a liquid glass capsule spans the width offered, its mode icons spread evenly across it. Open a mode and the capsule draws its leading edge back while a signal anchor carrying that mode's icon buds out of its leading end, born inside it, shrunk, and pulled out through a neck to rest joined beside it. Neither outer edge moves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The capsule trades its icons for the open mode's controls, which you build in `panel`: they blur in where the icons blurred out, on the reveal and dismiss roles. The panel gets the capsule's height (56pt) and the full width beside the anchor, so give its contents `maxWidth: .infinity` to span it, as the example's waveform, photos, chips and format buttons do; keep it plain content, since the capsule is already the glass. The example turns Voice into a live waveform and a running time, Photo into recent shots, Timer into duration chips and Text into format controls.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every change overlaps, so the body is never blank: opening, the panel blurs in as the icons blur out while the anchor buds; closing, the anchor melts home on the bounceless home spring and the icons start coming back 160ms in, while the capsule reaches back for it. The anchor keeps its glyph until it is inside. Setting `selection` from your code opens, closes or switches a mode the same way; switching swaps the panel and the anchor's glyph in place.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a selection tick as a mode opens, a soft impact as it closes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On iOS 26 the capsule and the anchor are Liquid Glass and the neck forms between them; before that they are frosted glass that simply sit side by side, and under Reduce Transparency they are solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the anchor fades in and out where it rests instead of budding, the capsule's edge moves on a short spring with no overshoot, and the icon and panel swaps cross-fade.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each mode icon is a button with its title; the anchor reads "Close" and the mode's title. Panels are your views, so give their controls labels.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`GlassModeBarStyle`) sets the icons' colour, the anchor's ink and the anchor's tint (signal by default). `Mode` is `GlassModeBarMode`: an `id`, an SF Symbol and a title. All text and symbols are semibold.

title: Glass Quick Add
description: A liquid glass Quick add pill that folds up into a card. Tap it and the pill grows up and across into a menu of capture kinds; pick one and the same glass re-forms in place into that capture, a title field and its option chips. A signal Save bubble buds out from under the card's corner only once there is something to save, melts back if the field empties, and saving folds the whole thing down into the pill.

contents.content: A capture kind in a `GlassQuickAdd`: its row in the menu, and what the capture asks for.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One glass card that changes what it is. At rest it is a Quick add pill. Tap it and it grows up and across into a card listing the capture kinds, each keyed by a tinted disc; pick one and the same glass re-forms in place into that kind's capture: a header with the kind and a close button, a title field (up to three lines) and the kind's option chips. The card's 26pt continuous corner makes the 52pt pill a capsule and the open card a rounded panel, so the shape never changes kind, only size, on the morph spring. Each stage's contents blur out as the next blur in.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: It grows from its lower trailing corner, so place it at the bottom of its space (a screen's bottom trailing corner, above a tab bar) and it opens upward.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Save is a signal bubble joined under the card's trailing corner. It buds out of the card the moment the field has text and melts back into the corner if the field empties, so it is only ever there when there is something to save. Saving (or Return) calls `onSave` with the kind, the trimmed text and the options that are on, then plays its own beat before anything closes: Save shows a spinner and morphs letter by letter to Saving, then turns sage with a check and Saved, with a success tap, then melts home and the card folds down into the pill. Each stage's contents leave quickly and the next arrive a beat later, so they never smear together as the glass resizes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The field takes focus as a capture opens, so the keyboard rises with it. Chips are plain content inside the card's glass: a soft fill, stronger when on; any number can be on.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass `stage` to open the menu or a capture from your code (`.closed`, `.menu`, `.capture(id)`), `text` to keep a draft or fill it in, and change `saveTrigger` to save from your code (a keyboard shortcut, a toolbar button) as if Save were tapped. Without them the piece keeps its own.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact as the pill opens, a success tap as Saved lands.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On iOS 26 the card and Save are Liquid Glass and Save's neck forms against the card; before that they are frosted glass, and under Reduce Transparency they are solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the card resizes on a short spring with no overshoot, Save fades in and out where it rests instead of budding, and the stage swaps cross-fade.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the pill, every kind, each chip (with its selected state), Close and Save are buttons; saving is announced. Text follows Dynamic Type.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`GlassQuickAddStyle`) sets the label, secondary, ink, action (Save) and success (Saved) colours. `Kind` (`GlassQuickAddKind`) sets each kind's id, symbol, title, prompt, options and disc tint. All text and symbols are semibold.

title: Glass Segments
description: A liquid glass segmented control: a signal-tinted glass indicator melted into a glass track as one surface. It moves like liquid, its leading edge reaching the new segment first and the trailing edge following, so it stretches across and gathers in. Grab it to scrub: it lifts under the finger, flattens against the ends and lands where the flick was heading, while the label ink flips exactly under its edge; tap still works.

contents.content: Visual tuning for `GlassSegments`. `standard` is a neutral glass track with a signal-tinted glass indicator melted into it, the house ink on the red; set `indicatorTint` for another tint.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Liquid glass: the track and the indicator are glass shapes in one liquid group (`GlassEffectContainer` on iOS 26). The track is neutral glass; the indicator is signal-tinted glass resting inside it, joined to it, so the two melt into one surface and the red reads as a lens of colour moving through the glass. The selected label sits on the red in the house ink, which reads on signal, sage and butter alike.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The indicator moves edge by edge. On a tap or an external change of `selection`, the edge facing the new segment leads on a quick spring and lands crisply while the far edge follows on a slightly slower one, so the indicator reaches across (about one and a third segments wide on a move to the neighbour) and gathers in to one segment with a little liquid give: the far edge passes its mark by about 3% of its travel and settles back. The leading edge never overshoots, so the indicator never pokes past the track at either end. Longer jumps stretch further (about two segments wide on a jump of three) and still land in under 0.4s.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A touch that lands on the indicator grabs it: it lifts (scale 1.04, deeper shadow) on a spring with no bounce and follows the finger directly, with no catch-up. Its leading edge reaches a little ahead with speed and relaxes when the finger rests. A touch anywhere else is a plain tap on that segment.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The indicator can be grabbed on the segment it is headed for while it is still moving there. It finishes that move under the finger instead of jumping to it, and the finger's own movement still applies directly.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Past either end, the edge at the wall gives no more than the 3pt track inset while the far edge follows against rubber-band resistance, so the indicator flattens against the end instead of leaving the track. The lift grows toward the wall there, so the lifted indicator stays inside the track too. The selection stays clamped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Release commits to the segment the flick would land on (`predictedEndLocation`), and both edges leave at the finger's speed into the same edge-by-edge hand-off. The lift comes down on the release spring as the indicator lands. Let go flattened against an end, it springs back to full width without the push.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One `.selection` haptic fires each time the indicator's center crosses into a new segment, once on tap, and once on release only if it lands somewhere new. Changes made through the binding are silent.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The binding changes on a short spring with no overshoot, so views that read the selection can animate with it, and a chart or a total switched by it never swings past its new value. A drag that a parent scroll view cancels puts the indicator back in its segment.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion removes the stretch, the reach, the flattening and the lift scale (the shadow still lifts): both edges move together on a short spring with no overshoot. Reduce Transparency draws the track and the indicator as opaque fills, the indicator still in its tint. Before iOS 26 both are frosted and simply don't merge.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Segments share the width equally; the control fills its container, so constrain it with `.frame(width:)` when you want it compact.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Labels are drawn twice: once in `Style.ink`, and once in `Style.selectedInk` masked to the indicator's live shape, so the color hands over exactly under the indicator edge while it moves, stretches or flattens. All type is semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `indicatorTint` sets the indicator's glass tint (`nil` is the house signal red; `.clear` leaves it neutral glass), and `GlassSegmentsStyle.block(_:)` makes one in another tint with dark ink.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The example floats the control over a few color blocks, since glass over a flat page reads as grey.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`GlassSegments.Style`, alias of `GlassSegmentsStyle`): `ink`, `selectedInk`, `indicatorTint`, `font`, `disabledOpacity`; `track` and `indicatorSurface` are kept for existing code but no longer used, since both shapes are glass. `.disabled(true)` fades the control and ignores touches. The row height scales with Dynamic Type (capped at 1.5x).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a floating tab bar whose lens follows the finger, see the Pro Lessons screen (`lens-tab-bar`).

title: Glass Surface
description: The public face of the SwiftPieces liquid glass: `.glassSurface` draws any view on a liquid glass capsule, rect, circle or concentric shape, and `GlassSurface.Group` melts neighbouring surfaces into one through a liquid neck. Liquid Glass on iOS 26; before it a frosted surface with its own press, top light and specular edge; a solid fill under Reduce Transparency, and a designed disabled state everywhere.

contents.content: The SwiftPieces liquid glass, for your own views: Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a layered frosted surface everywhere else, with the same press feel on both. `.glassSurface` draws the same glass every SwiftPieces piece is made of, and `GlassSurface.Group` is the same liquid group: surfaces inside one that come within its `spacing` of each other melt into one shape through a neck. Rest the parts of one control 6pt apart, so the neck holds, and separate actions 26pt apart, so each is its own bubble. Text and symbols on a surface take the house weight, semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: This is the SwiftPieces liquid glass, for your own views. `.glassSurface` draws the same glass every piece is made of, and `GlassSurface.Group(spacing:)` is the same liquid group: on iOS 26 a `GlassEffectContainer`, so surfaces within `spacing` of each other melt into one shape through a neck that pinches as they separate and snaps when they pass it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Rest the parts of one control 6pt apart, inside the merge distance, so the neck holds (a transport's previous, play and next, as in the example); rest separate actions 26pt apart, so each is its own bubble. Put every surface of one piece of UI in one group, never one group inside another, and never one surface on top of another.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On iOS 26 this is real Liquid Glass; `tint` tints it natively. Earlier it is a frosted fill with a light rim, a top light and a specular edge (a bright top highlight plus a faint `.primary` edge); a tint lies over it at `Style.tintAmount`. Under Reduce Transparency it is opaque: `Style.solidFill` (the secondary system background by default) with the tint on top.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tint only to say something: the house signal red for the primary action, sage for success, butter for a warning. Ink on a tinted surface reads best in the house ink (#141414); on neutral glass, let it follow the appearance.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Text and symbols on a surface take the house weight, semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `interactive: true` on iOS 26 is the system's interactive glass, which swells under the finger and owns the press; the surface adds no motion or haptic on top of it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On the fallback, `interactive: true` gives the pane a press of its own. It sinks level to `Style.pressedScale` (0.96) on a tight spring with no overshoot, its far shadow draws in close under it, and light pools under the finger and follows it. On lift it springs back up on the shared release spring, passing rest by about 8% of the press depth before it settles, and the shadow swings back out with it. A finger that slides more than 44pt off the edge lets go without the give, and the press returns if the finger comes back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One light impact plays as a tap lifts on the fallback surface, never on touch-down, so touches that turn into scrolls stay silent. A touch that travels more than 44pt before it lifts (a drag, a slider scrub, a slide from one button to another) ends without it. The press is tracked with a simultaneous gesture, so a `Button` inside still owns the tap, and a touch the system cancels (a scroll taking over) releases the surface instead of leaving it pressed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Lift: on iOS 26 a lone surface floats on a wide, faint shadow in light mode (`Style.shadow`); inside a group the group floats its surfaces as one instead. In dark mode the glass carries its own depth.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion drops the fallback's scale and the release's give. The light pool, the closer shadow and the haptic stay, so the press still reads.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.concentric(minimum:)` resolves to `ConcentricRectangle` on iOS 26 (set `.containerShape` on the parent) and to a continuous rounded rect with `minimum` as the radius earlier.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`.standard`): `tintAmount` (0.72, so a tinted fallback reads as a color block), `specular`, `shadow`, `pressedScale` (0.96), `disabledOpacity` and `solidFill` for Reduce Transparency.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Disabled: `.disabled(true)` fades and desaturates the surface and silences the press response on both paths.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a floating glass card over full-bleed art with detents, see the Pro Stay screen (`glass-sheet`).

title: Address Field
description: A liquid glass address field for checkout, delivery and sign-up. Type-ahead suggestions pour down out of the field as a glass list with the matched text picked out, a clear or searching bubble buds from the field's end, and picking a row with a tap or the hardware keyboard buds a spinner bubble beside it while it resolves into a structured address with street, city, state, postal code, country and coordinate; the list then melts back into the field as the address settles in with the locality on a second line and a sage check, keeping the typed text usable with a "Use as typed" row and a butter retry bubble when a lookup fails.

contents.content: Address entry with type-ahead suggestions that resolve to a structured, verified address. The field is a liquid glass shape, and what it shows buds out of it: the suggestion list pours down out of the field and rests apart from it, the clear (or searching) bubble comes out of its end, and the bubble that spins while a pick resolves comes out of the list beside the chosen row. Each melts back into where it came from. Typing searches after a short pause (three characters or more). Each new keystroke cancels the search in flight, so a slow answer for an older query never replaces a newer one. Picking a suggestion looks up the full address; when it arrives, `address` is set, `text` becomes the address's first line (usually the street) and the locality shows under it. Editing the text again clears `address`. Location permission is never requested: suggestions come from the query alone, optionally biased by `region`. `swift @State private var query = "" @State private var address: AddressField.Address? AddressField("Delivery address", text: $query, address: $address, countries: ["US", "CA"]) `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The field is a liquid glass shape (Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a frosted fallback before it, a solid fill under Reduce Transparency), and what it shows buds out of it and melts back in. The suggestion list pours down out of the field and rests apart from it, 26pt below. A round bubble as tall as the field buds from the field's end while you edit: it spins while suggestions load and is a clear button otherwise. While that bubble is out the field gives it its end, and the list follows the field's edge, so the two stay in line with the bubble's column beside them. `Style.field` tints the glass; `.clear`, the default, leaves it neutral.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Typing searches once the trimmed text is three characters or more, after a 250ms pause. The search runs in a task keyed on the text, so every keystroke cancels the one in flight: a slow answer for an older query can never replace a newer list. Earlier suggestions stay on screen while the next ones load, with the field's bubble spinning instead of a flicker.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Suggestions come from `MKLocalSearchCompleter` with `resultTypes = .address`, at most five, with the matched runs in the label colour, the rest of the title in the secondary colour, and the locality on a second line. Picking one runs an `MKLocalSearch` for that completion: the other rows dim and a spinner bubble buds out of the list's end beside the chosen row. Picking another row, editing the text or leaving the screen cancels the lookup, and a late answer is ignored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Once resolved, `address` holds the street, city, state, postal code, country, ISO country code, coordinate and a single line formatted for the address's own country. `text` becomes the first line (usually the street), the rest shows under it in the field and a sage check lands inside the field. `mailingLines` gives the label lines in the country's postal order.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Editing the text clears `address`. Setting `address` from outside (a saved address) fills the field without searching, and its check lands on a short spring with no success pop or haptic; setting `text` and `address` together is not treated as an edit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A failed lookup stays on its row: the row's pin turns into a butter warning mark, the message replaces the locality, and the spinner bubble beside it turns butter with a retry arrow; tapping the bubble or the row tries again. A failed suggestion request shows "Couldn't load suggestions" with the same butter retry bubble beside it. No matches is a quiet line. In each of these cases a "Use as typed" row sets an address with `isVerified == false` holding only the typed text. Turn it off with `allowsUnverified: false`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `countries: ["US", "CA"]` leaves out suggestions whose last line names another country, and a picked address outside the list shows "Choose an address in United States" on its row instead of being set, with no retry bubble since trying again gives the same answer. `region` biases suggestions toward an area. Location permission is never requested.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: iOS 26 moves map items to `MKAddress`, which has no separate street or postal code, and deprecates `MKPlacemark`. On iOS 17 to 25 the parts come from the placemark; on iOS 26 from the item's placemark read dynamically (so the file builds without deprecation warnings), with `MKAddressRepresentations` for the formatted line, city and country as the fallback.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `source:` swaps MapKit for your own backend, or a fixed list for previews and tests. Both calls are cancelled when their result is no longer wanted.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hardware keyboard: up and down arrows move the highlight, Return picks the highlighted row (or the top one), Escape closes the list. A long street wraps up to three lines. A pasted multi-line address is joined with commas.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The list sits inline under the field and pushes content down, so it scrolls with a form and never clips inside a scroll view. Leaving the field hides it; coming back shows it again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Motion: the list is born as a thin sliver tucked inside the field's bottom edge and springs down to its place, growing to full height as the neck between them stretches and snaps; its room in the layout opens with it, so what sits below glides down. Going home it reaches back up, melts into the field on a spring with no bounce, and only then leaves the layout, its rows gone the moment it heads back. As it refines while you type it resizes without overshoot, so nothing below it wobbles, and typing itself is never animated or delayed. Bubbles bud out of their parent's end on the same cycle, their glyphs blurring in just after they leave and out the moment they head home, and a glyph that changes inside a bubble (spinner to clear, spinner to retry) blurs from one to the other. A row's highlight wash is there on touch-down, the row sinks about a point, and the wash fades as the finger lifts; bubbles sink too and spring back. When a pick resolves, the spinner and the list melt home as the street and locality settle into the field, which grows for the second line with a little give, and the sage check lands on the expressive spring as the success haptic plays.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Type is one weight, semibold, for the text, rows and every glyph; size and colour set the hierarchy.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the field's hint says whether the address is verified; the suggestion count ("5 suggestions", inflected), "Finding address", the result and any error are announced; rows are buttons read as title and locality with the selected trait when highlighted. The clear bubble is "Clear address"; a failed suggestion request's bubble is "Retry suggestions".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact on picking a suggestion, success when the address resolves, error when a lookup fails, selection ticks for arrow-key moves. "Use as typed" sets the address at once, so it plays only the success. Nothing per keystroke.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: rows and the field grow and wrap; at accessibility sizes the leading glyphs step aside so titles get the width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the field tint, label, secondary label, focus ring, row highlight, success, error (the warning mark and the retry bubble) and ink colors, the pin, optional suggestion tiles, the corner radius and the minimum height (also the bubbles' size).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the list and bubbles fade in and out in place instead of budding, glyph changes fade, and pressed rows and buttons dim instead of sinking. Highlights, the dimmed rows during a lookup, the spinners, colors, announcements and haptics are unchanged. Reduce Transparency draws the field, list and bubbles as solid shapes.

title: Amount Field
description: A currency amount entry that formats live in the user's locale as each digit lands (grouping, decimal separator, symbol before or after, the currency's own fraction digits), with a large auto-fitting semibold figure whose digits roll in, a blinking signal caret right after the digits, robust paste of amounts like "$1,234.56" or "1 234,56 €", and a limit that refuses the keystroke with a damped shake, an error haptic and a butter glass pill with the limit, budding out of the compact field's liquid glass block, all backed by a `Decimal` binding.

contents.content: Currency amount entry with live locale formatting, a `Decimal` value and a limit. The field keeps its own digit buffer and renders the formatted string itself, so the caret never jumps and locale separators never break parsing. Formatting follows `\.locale`; fraction digits come from the currency. The figure is content and stays on your ground. The compact block is a liquid glass shape, and the limit shows on a butter glass pill: it buds down out of the compact block and melts back into it, and rises in under the hero figure, which has no glass of its own to come from.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The field keeps its own buffer of typed digits and renders the formatted string itself. A hidden `TextField` with `.decimalPad` captures keys, so the caret never jumps and grouping separators never reach a parser. The caret, in the signal red, is drawn right after the digits, before a trailing symbol ("1.234,56| €"), and blinks with a short fade like the system caret, turning solid whenever the amount changes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The value is a `Decimal`. Fraction digits come from the currency through `Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency`: JPY takes none, USD two, KWD three. Formatting follows `\.locale`, so `.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "de_DE"))` gives "1.234,56 €", en\_IN groups in lakhs ("₹1,23,456") and ar\_SA shows Arabic-Indic digits.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While typing, what you typed is what you see: "12." keeps its separator and "12.50" keeps its zero. Leading zeros are stripped, "." on an empty field starts "0.", a second separator is ignored and digits past the currency's precision are dropped. Leaving the field settles "12.5" to "12.50" and "12." to "12".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Both "." and "," (and the Arabic decimal separator) work as the decimal key, whatever the device region. Digits in any script are accepted and stored as ASCII.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Paste (long-press, or Command-V) parses "1,234.56", "$99", "1 234,56 €", "US$ 12" and Arabic-Indic text. A lone separator followed by exactly three digits reads as thousands unless the currency has three decimals. Words, two numbers or a minus sign are refused like a key past the limit, with a shake and an error haptic but no limit pill; one already showing stays.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `limit` refuses the keystroke or paste that would pass it with one firm knock: the figure (or the compact block and its ring) shakes once with an `.error` haptic on the same beat, VoiceOver announces the limit, and the `limitMessage` arrives a beat behind the knock on a butter glass pill with house ink, then goes after a moment. The same refusal repeated less than a second apart, like a key pressed again and again at the limit, gets a half-height shake and a lighter tap instead of escalating. Accepted keys stay quiet. An external value over the limit is shown as it is, not clamped, with the pill and (compact) a butter ring; the digits keep their colour so they stay readable on a light ground.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: External writes to the binding (a quick-amount chip, a reset) redraw the display at the currency's precision. Negative or over-precise values are normalized and written back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.hero` is a large semibold figure that scales down to fit its width, with digits rolling in through `.numericText()` on a spring that never overshoots, so a digit never rolls past its place. The fit uses the same spring, so the figure shrinks while a digit rolls in and never swells past its width, and typing never waits on an animation. The figure is content and sits on your ground; the limit pill rises in under it. Both follow Dynamic Type.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.compact` is a 56pt liquid glass block (Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a frosted fallback before it) with a focus ring. Its limit pill buds down out of the block and rests joined to it, 6pt below, so a liquid neck holds the two; when the limit has had its say the words go, the butter drains and the pill melts back into the block. The pill's room in the layout opens and closes with it, so what sits below glides rather than jumps. `Style.field` tints the block; `.clear`, the default, leaves it neutral.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Type is one weight, semibold, for the caption, the figure and the pill; size alone sets the hierarchy.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The example's quick-amount chips are neutral glass capsules resting joined, so they read as one liquid strip; they write the binding like any external value.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the label and the full formatted amount as the value ("$1,234.56"), and the limit as a hint. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and blocks focus. `isFocused` lets you raise or dismiss the keyboard.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the block tint, amount, secondary label, caret, error (the pill's tint and the over-limit ring) and ink (the pill's text) colors, plus the compact block's height and corner radius.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no shake; each refusal dims the digits for a beat with the same haptic, digit changes crossfade, and the limit pill fades in and out in place, still clearing itself after a moment. Reduce Transparency draws the block and the pill as solid shapes.
