title: Date Range Picker
description: A start-to-end date range picker on a paged month grid built from the environment calendar and locale, with the selection in liquid glass over the grid. A touch presses a small glass bubble into the day and the tap swells it into a red glass start bubble; the second tap lands the end the same way and the band pours out of the start along each week and into the end like liquid, joined to both bubbles by necks. Sold-out days are struck through, a refused end day swells into a butter bubble that shakes and melts away, a maximum length dims unreachable days, months page by swipe or a joined pair of glass chevrons that melt into each other at the ends, the month and summary morph letter by letter, and a glass chip reads out the dates and nights.

contents.content: Day-granular start/end range picker with a paged month grid. The selection is always two start-of-day dates in the environment `Calendar` and `TimeZone` (`upperBound` is the start of the last day, e.g. the check-out day for a stay). The first tap sets a start, the second closes the range (a day before the start becomes the new start), and a third tap starts over. A range can never contain a disabled or out-of-bounds day: an end tap that would span one, or that exceeds `maximumLength`, is refused with an error haptic, a butter bubble that flares and shakes on the tapped day and a short notice, and the start stays in place. The grid stays as it is and the selection is liquid glass over it: the start and end are tinted bubbles, and the band between them is liquid glass that joins them through a neck at each end and wraps across week rows.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The selection is a `ClosedRange<Date>` of start-of-day dates in the environment `Calendar` and `TimeZone`. `upperBound` is the start of the last day (the check-out day for a stay). Dates you pass in are normalized to their day.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: First tap sets the start and clears any old range, second tap sets the end, third tap starts a new range. Tapping a day before the pending start moves the start there. In `.nights` mode tapping the start again cancels it; in `.days` mode it confirms a one-day range.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The grid stays as it is and the selection is liquid glass over it. Touching a day presses a small clear glass bubble into it. The tap that makes it the start or end swells that bubble out to full size on a spring that springs a little past it, its red flooding in, so the press and the landing are one bubble; with no finger behind it (a VoiceOver tap, a range set from outside) it swells and fades in where it lands. A bubble whose day stops being an endpoint drains clear and shrinks away where it is, without bounce. Pressing a day that already has a bubble sinks it and it springs back with a little bounce. The day's number turns to dark ink as the red comes in, so it reads on the red. The glass is drawn behind the day buttons, so a press never dims or dents it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A range never contains an unavailable day. An end tap that would span a day marked by `isDateDisabled` or outside `bounds`, or that exceeds `maximumLength`, is refused: the start stays, an `.error` haptic plays, the bubble under the finger swells into butter glass (`Style.error`) as the day shakes once, holds for a beat and melts away, and the summary chip turns butter with the notice ("Includes unavailable dates", "Up to 14 nights") for two seconds, or until the next tap closes or restarts the range. The flare and shake also mark the refusal with `showsSummary: false`. While a start is pending, days that cannot close the range fade to a dim, and fade back when it closes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The grid comes from the calendar: `firstWeekday`, days per week, days in the month and the weekday offset all come from `Calendar` APIs, so Hebrew, Islamic, Ethiopic and other calendars lay out correctly. Weekday symbols are the calendar's very short standalone symbols; day numbers, month titles and the summary use `Date.FormatStyle` and `Date.IntervalFormatStyle` in the environment locale, including native digits.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Day math uses `Calendar.date(byAdding:)` and counts days on civil dates, never 86,400 second steps, so 23 and 25 hour DST days and time zones whose midnight is skipped stay exact.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The band is liquid glass that joins the start and end bubbles: it rests a few points short of each, so a liquid neck holds it to both (a red bubble and the neutral band blend through the neck), and it wraps across week rows as one capsule per week, with rounded ends at row and month edges. Each week row is its own liquid group, so the band in one week never melts into the next. When a range completes, the band pours out of the start bubble like one pen stroke: a drop that lengthens into the band, filling each week in turn as the pen reaches it, quick off the start and easing into the end bubble, in at most half a second, where the neck snaps in. The end bubble lands at once and never waits for the band. Starting a new range drains the old band back along the same path into its start on a spring with no bounce, while its bubbles drain and shrink away and the new start swells in. Offsets follow the layout direction, so right to left the grid, the band and the bubbles all flow right to left.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Months page with the chevrons or a horizontal swipe (a paging `ScrollView` with its native fling, which runs out to the card's edges so a month slides in from the edge), and the month title morphs letter by letter without overshoot. The chevrons are a joined pair of glass bubbles; at the first or last month the one that can't page melts into the other, and buds back out as soon as it can, each keeping its place. They scroll to the month on a short spring that settles with a little give. Paging stops at the months of `bounds`; without bounds it spans five years either side of today and the selection's month.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The summary shows the range in the locale's interval pattern ("Mar 4 – 9") and one glass chip: "Select end date" while a start waits for its end, the notice after a refusal (tinted butter), and the length in `counting` units once the range closes, pluralized with automatic grammar agreement. The chip morphs between them, its label changing letter by letter and its glass widening or narrowing around it. It pops with a bounce when a tap closes the range, on the beat of the success haptic; a range set from outside, which plays no haptic, lands it on a short spring instead. The dates morph letter by letter without overshoot.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: `.selection` when a start is set, `.success` when a range completes, `.error` on a refused end. One per tap; nothing plays on press.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each day is a button labeled with its full date ("Tuesday, March 4", plus the year outside the current one, and "Today" first for today), with the `.isSelected` trait inside the range and a value of Start date, End date, In range or Unavailable. Month changes, completed ranges and refusals are announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: day cells grow with `@ScaledMetric` from 44pt up to 76pt tall, and the bubbles and band with them; day numbers scale to accessibility sizes and shrink to fit rather than clip. The summary stacks when it no longer fits on one line, and at accessibility sizes the titles and the chip wrap and blur across instead of morphing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no pour, swelling, shake, overshoot or morph. Bubbles, the chevrons and the band fade in and out where they rest, a pressed bubble shades instead of sinking (darker in light mode, lighter in dark), a refused day still flares butter, titles cross-fade, and out-of-reach days still fade. The swipe no longer slides the grid; both the swipe and the chevrons crossfade to the next month, and a short quick flick pages as well as a drag past 50pt. Reduce Transparency draws the glass solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the ground, day text, muted text, the glass tints of the band (neutral by default), the start and end bubbles (the signal red) and the month buttons (neutral), ink on tinted glass, the today dot, disabled days, and the butter tint of the notice and the refusal flare. `cornerRadius` no longer does anything: the bubbles are round and the band a capsule. `.disabled(true)` dims the picker and stops taps and paging.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For booking a time slot inside a day, see the slot picker in SwiftPieces Pro.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Bound range, or `nil` while nothing (or only a start) is chosen. In `.nights` mode it stays `nil` until the end is tapped; in `.days` mode a lone start already reads as a one-day range.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `bounds`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: First and last selectable days. Days outside are muted and inert, and paging stops at their months. `nil` allows any day and pages five years either side of today.

contents.heading: parameters

contents.content: Longest allowed range, counted in `counting` units. While a start is pending, days that cannot close the range are dimmed.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `.days` counts both ends (Mar 4 to Mar 9 is 6 days, and a single day is allowed). `.nights` counts nights (5 nights, and the end must be after the start).

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Colors. Defaults to the SwiftPieces house palette (red glass start and end bubbles with dark ink, joined by a neutral glass band), adapting to light and dark.

title: Expanding Track
description: A thumbless liquid glass slider: a glass bar that swells from 8pt to a 32pt bar under the finger with a solid color fill inside, shows detent dots while dragging, buds a glass readout bubble up out of the bar that rides the held edge on a liquid neck and melts back in when you let go, squishes past either end, and can carry an uppercase label with a big numeral; a second init selects a range with two sinking handles.

contents.content: Thumbless liquid glass slider that swells under the finger. Bind a `Double` for a single value or a `ClosedRange<Double>` for a range. The bar is a glass shape with the fill inside it. While you drag an untitled track, the value buds up out of the bar on a glass bubble that rides the held edge, joined to the bar by a liquid neck, and melts back in on release.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: There is no thumb: the whole 44pt row is the hit area and the value follows the finger's x position directly, so the bar can rest at 8pt and still be easy to grab. Tracking is never animated: from the first touch, including a tap far from the current value, the edge of the fill sits under the finger. With a `step`, the value snaps from step to step beneath it while the edge stays with the finger, and on release the edge lands on its step with a little give. A VoiceOver step or a change from your code glides the fill (and the range handles) onto the new value on the same spring.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The bar is liquid glass carrying the fill as a solid block, with the detent dots and handles. While held it inflates to 32pt (`Style.activeHeight`) on a quick spring with no overshoot, and the dots at each `step` fade in a beat behind it, so they never show through a thin bar. On release they fade first and the bar settles back to 8pt with a little give. The swell runs on its own spring, apart from the fill edge, the squish and the landing, and a drag moves offsets and masks rather than resizing the fill.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Without a `title`, the value buds up out of the bar on a glass bubble the moment you touch it. The bubble rides the held edge, kept over the bar, and rests a liquid neck's width above it, so the two stay joined while you drag. Let go and it melts back into the bar, its number blurring away as it heads home. The bubble draws above the track's frame, so leave a little room above an untitled track.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass `title` for the labeled layout: an uppercase caption with the value as a big numeral above the track, decimals dimmed at the locale's separator. The numeral rolls to a new value after a programmatic or VoiceOver change, without overshooting it, and updates directly while you drag, so it stays legible under the finger. A titled track reads its value there, so it buds no bubble.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pushing past either end, the bar gives toward the far end with rubber-band resistance, never more than about 24pt, and bulges slightly across, like silicone pressed against a stop. The value stays at the bound, and the readout bubble stays over the end of the bar as it gives. On release it springs back at the speed the finger was pushing. Push past the end again while it is still springing back and it eases onto the finger from where it is drawn instead of jumping.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a selection tick per `step` crossing (every tenth of the span without a step), and a rigid impact when the value reaches a bound, in place of that step's tick. No haptic is added for the press or release itself; a touch-down that moves the value plays that change's tick or impact. The optional symbol lights while held and plays `.variableColor` when the value rises past a tick.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The range init keeps the handles apart by `minimumDistance` and lets the active ink handle sink into the fill; VoiceOver gets separate "Minimum" and "Maximum" adjustable elements, prefixed with the title when there is one.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A drag the system cancels lets go exactly like a release, so the bar never stays swollen and the bubble always melts back in.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` carries the bar's glass tint (`trough`, neutral glass by default), the fill block, ink, labels and track metrics. `.standard` is the house palette (a brand red fill in neutral glass); pass `.init(fill:)` to use another block. All text is semibold. `.disabled(true)` greys the fill.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the bar stays at 8pt and its fill darkens a step while held (brightens in dark mode) instead of swelling, the readout bubble opens and closes in place above the held edge instead of budding, the ends stop the bar without any give, the edge lands on its step and glides to a new value on a short spring with no overshoot, and the numeral changes without rolling. Haptics, the symbol tint and its pulse are unchanged. Reduce Transparency draws the glass as solid shapes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The drag starts on touch-down so the track responds to taps; inside a vertical `ScrollView` or sheet, a drag that begins on the track moves the value rather than scrolling.

title: Filter Rail
description: A scrolling rail of liquid glass filter chips with optional counts, resting apart as their own bubbles. Single-select marks the pick with a brand red glass puck that stretches between chips, its leading edge first, melting into each chip it crosses while every label turns to dark ink exactly under its edge; multi-select picks take the red tint with a check, file to the leading edge, and a counting Clear chip buds out of the first pick and melts back into the rail when cleared; the chosen chip scrolls into view, and edges fade only when content overflows.

contents.content: Horizontal rail of liquid glass chips bound to a `Set` of selected titles. The chips are glass bubbles resting apart. Single-select marks the pick with a tinted glass puck that stretches between chips and melts into each one it crosses; multi-select tints each pick, and a Clear chip buds out of the first pick to clear them all.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every chip is a liquid glass capsule. Chips are separate choices, so they rest apart, outside the distance at which glass melts together, and only goo while something crosses or buds from them.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Single-select marks the pick with one glass puck tinted `Style.indicator`, the brand red by default. At rest the selected chip carries the tint itself, so it moves with the chip through any layout change, such as counts refreshing. On a new pick the puck lifts off and travels edge by edge: the edge facing the new chip leads on a snap spring and the far edge follows a beat later on a slightly looser one, so the puck stretches toward the pick (by about an eighth of the jump) and gathers in on it, melting into each chip it crosses on the way. The edges move in points, so the pace stays even across chips of different widths. It lands with a little give, each edge a few percent of the jump past its mark, and settles without wobbling, and a pick made while it is still landing retargets it smoothly. At the first or last chip the rail's end stops the leading edge, so the puck squashes against the end with its round cap intact. Once the far edge settles, the new chip takes the tint back. Tapping the selected chip again keeps it selected, so include an "All" option if you need a neutral state.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While the puck travels, every label is drawn twice, in the chip's ink outside the puck and in `Style.onIndicator` inside it, so a label turns exactly under the puck's edge as it passes instead of crossfading. If a `Set` with several titles reaches a single-select rail, the puck sits on the first of them in `options` order.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Multi-select tints each picked chip's glass and blurs a check into it. The tint comes on as the press springs back, so a pick clicks on in one motion. Tints come from `Style.blocks` by option position, so a chip keeps its color wherever it moves; the house palette is the one brand red, since a pick is a selection. Picks file to the leading edge first and the rest of the chips make room a beat after. A chip that travels far can carry its give a little into the gap as it lands, and slips under its neighbor rather than over: a new pick under the chip before it, a deselected chip under the chip after it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The first pick buds a glass Clear chip out of the leading end of the first chip, into room the rail opens for it, with a count of the picks that rolls as it changes. Clearing lets every pick go together and the Clear chip melts back into the chip that slides to the front as the room closes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `counts` adds a result count after each title; VoiceOver reads it as the chip's value.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Selection changes set `scrollPosition(id:)`, so the chosen chip centers itself (single) or the rail returns to its leading edge (multi). The scroll follows a beat behind on a calmer spring, so it never stacks with the puck into one lurch.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Edge fades are computed from the content frame in a named coordinate space, so they show only on the side that actually has chips hidden. The rail keeps a 44pt row; the glass's shadows draw above and below it uncut, so give it room in a tight stack.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Chips use the shared press: they sink a few points on touch-down with no bounce and spring back on release. Pressing the selected chip sinks the puck and its ink with it. All text is semibold. `.disabled(true)` dims the whole rail. One selection haptic fires for every change to the bound set, including changes made from outside.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion the puck slides on a short spring with no overshoot and no stretch, the scroll follows on that same short spring, the check fades and the Clear chip opens and closes in place instead of budding, and a pressed chip (or the puck) shades instead of sinking. The ink handover, the tints and the haptic stay. Reduce Transparency draws the glass as solid shapes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a searchable list of commands instead of a rail, see the Command Palette screen in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Form Field
description: A liquid glass text field whose label rests inside as a placeholder and glides up into a caption on focus or once filled, with an optional leading icon and help text. A clear bubble buds out of the field's end while you type, a character counter buds down out of it and turns butter at a grapheme-accurate limit, bumping when extra input is refused, and validation waits until you leave the field before drawing an error ring and budding a butter warning bubble with the message, an error haptic and a VoiceOver announcement, shakes the field once when Return or a form submit meets an error, and shows a quiet sage check once fixed.

contents.content: Text field with a floating label, help and error text, a character limit and a counter. The field is a liquid glass shape. Whatever appears because of it buds out of it and melts back in: the clear button out of its end while you type, the counter out of its bottom edge while it is focused or filled, and the warning bubble that carries an error message. The bubbles rest joined to the field, so a liquid neck holds them. Chain fields by applying `.focused($focus, equals: .email)` to each `FormField` (focus reaches the text field inside) and moving focus in `onSubmit`. Apply `SwiftUI/View/formFieldRevealsErrors(_:)` to a form to show every field's validation at once, for example after a submit button is tapped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The field is a liquid glass shape (Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a frosted fallback before it, a solid fill under Reduce Transparency). Everything that appears because of it buds out of it and melts back in, and rests joined to it, 6pt away, so a liquid neck holds the two: the clear button out of its end, the counter out of its bottom edge, and the warning bubble that carries an error. Each bubble is born inside the field, springs out pulling the neck thin, and goes home on a spring with no bounce, its glyph or label gone the moment it heads back. `Style.field` tints the glass; `.clear`, the default, leaves it neutral.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The label is one `Text` in `.body` that moves between two alignments and scales down into a reserved caption slot. The scale is the caption-to-body line-height ratio at the current Dynamic Type size, so the label lands in the same place at every size, including the accessibility sizes, with no font swap and no jump.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `prompt` shows only while the field is focused and empty, under the floated label. The system placeholder is suppressed so the label is never drawn twice.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The clear button is a round glass bubble as tall as the field. It buds out of the field's end while the field is focused and holds text: the field's trailing edge pulls back on the bud's own spring and the bubble parts from it through a neck, so the whole control keeps its width. It sinks slightly under the finger, clears at once and keeps the keyboard up, then melts back into the field.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `limit` counts extended grapheme clusters (`String.count`), so a flag, a family emoji or a letter with a combining accent is one character. Typing or pasting past the limit trims with `prefix(limit)`, which never cuts a character in half. The counter is `count/limit` on a glass capsule that buds down out of the field while it is focused or holds text, with localized digits that roll without overshoot. At the limit the capsule floods `Style.error` (butter) with ink digits, and a refused keystroke fires a light impact as the counter swells and rebounds, a value pushed against its bound. The counter's place is kept while it is home, so reaching the limit or the counter coming and going never shifts the help text; while the clear bubble holds the column beside the field, the counter moves in with the field's end so it stays under the field. The trim runs a frame after an over-limit edit, and the counter never shows that frame's count. With an IME that composes text (Japanese, Chinese), trimming can end a composition early when it runs past the limit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Validation timing: `.onBlur` (default) waits until the field has been edited and left, `.onSubmit` waits for Return, `.live` starts with the first edit. After that the field validates on every keystroke, so the error clears the moment the text is fixed and a sage check blurs in quietly inside the field. Once validation has started the check keeps its slot while the field has text, so typing never reflows as the text turns valid or invalid. An empty field gives the slot back, so its resting label keeps the full width. An `error` passed from outside shows immediately and takes priority.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `formFieldRevealsErrors(true)` on a container arms every field inside, for a Save button that should flag untouched required fields. Each field holding an error as it turns on shakes once. It is a `Bool`, so a second tap while it is already on does not shake again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: When an error first appears the ring turns `Style.error`, the help text blurs away, and a butter bubble with an exclamation mark buds down out of the field's leading corner with the message arriving beside it a beat behind the ring; an `.error` haptic plays once. When the message changes while an error is showing, the new text blurs in place. When the error is fixed the message goes, the bubble melts back into the field, and the help text returns once it is home.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A refused submit shakes the field once, with the `.error` haptic on the same beat: Return pressed while the field has an error, or `formFieldRevealsErrors` turning on. The bubbles under it hold still, so their necks stretch with the shake. An error found while typing or when you leave the field never shakes; the ring and the warning bubble carry it. One haptic per event: a new error plays it as it appears, and a refusal of an error already on screen plays its own. A Return whose `onSubmit` also turns `formFieldRevealsErrors` on is one submit, with one shake and one haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Focus: apply `.focused($focus, equals: .email)` to the `FormField` itself and move focus in `onSubmit`, with `submitLabel: .next`. Tapping anywhere on the field, including the icon and padding, focuses it. The ring, icon and label answer focus together on one short spring that lands with only a hint of give.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `axis: .vertical` grows up to eight lines. Return inserts a newline there, so `onSubmit` does not fire; put a multiline field last in a chain. The clear bubble sits level with the field's top.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.emailAddress` and `.URL` keyboards (and email, URL and username content types) turn off autocapitalization and autocorrection.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Type is one weight, semibold, for the label, the text, the help, the counter and every glyph; size alone sets the hierarchy.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the label, the text with the counter ("12 of 160 characters") as the value, and the error or help as the hint. A new or changed error is announced. The clear bubble is a button labelled "Clear" with the field's label. The floating label, icon, check and footer are hidden to avoid double reading.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the field tint, label, secondary, focus ring, error, success and ink colors plus minimum height (44pt floor, also the clear bubble's size) and corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and calls the clear bubble home.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Typing never waits on motion: nothing animates the typed text, and the check turning on or off never moves the input or caret.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: bubbles fade in and out in place instead of budding, the label still moves (it is the state change) but on a short spring with no bounce, the check and messages fade instead of blurring, and the counter fades between counts instead of rolling. A refused keystroke dims the counter for a beat instead of swelling it. A refused submit plays its haptic and dims the error ring for a beat instead of shaking, so a Return on an error already showing still shows on screen. The clear button dims instead of sinking. Reduce Transparency draws the field and bubbles as solid shapes.

title: Location Picker
description: A map picker for delivery, rides, events and listings: drag the map under a fixed red pin that lifts while the map moves and, when it settles, drops and presses into place with a light tap, the address under it is looked up after a short pause with stale answers cancelled and recent ones cached. The chrome over the map is liquid glass: a floating glass card shows the street and locality, morphing letter by letter as it changes (a dropped pin with coordinates where there is no address, and a Retry bubble that pinches off its end when the lookup fails), the glass locate button asks for location only when tapped and flies to you, and the red Confirm capsule buds down out of the card once the spot has its answer and melts back into it while the map moves.

contents.content: A map you drag under a fixed pin to choose an exact spot, with the address of wherever the pin lands. The pin stays in the middle of the visible map. While the map moves it lifts and its shadow spreads; when the map settles it drops and presses into place, `selection` is set to the coordinate, and the address is looked up after a short pause. A newer settle cancels the lookup in flight, so an address never lands on the wrong spot, and recent answers are cached by position (about 5 m), so nudging back costs no request. Location permission is only requested when the locate button is tapped. `swift @State private var place: LocationPicker.Place? LocationPicker(selection: $place, initialCenter: store.coordinate) { place in order.dropOff = place } `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The picker takes the size it is given, at least 320 pt tall: full screen, in a sheet, or `.frame(height: 340).clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 26))` inside a form. Bind `selection`, and pass `onConfirm` for the Confirm button. Add `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` to your Info.plist for the locate button. Full screen, the map already runs under the status bar and the home indicator while the card and the locate button stay clear of them, so leave out `.ignoresSafeArea()`, which would push both under the system bars.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The pin stays in the middle of the map the card leaves visible. While the map moves it lifts 12 pt, its shadow spreads and a small mark stays on the exact spot. Picked up by your drag, it springs about a point past its lift and settles; a flight (locate, a VoiceOver move, a new selection) lifts it on a short spring. When the map settles it drops on a spring that never overshoots, so the tip stops on the spot instead of sinking through it, then gives a little from the tip as it meets the ground and springs back into shape, with a light tap on that beat. Only a real change of the spot under the pin lifts it, so the camera reports MapKit sends on appear, on rotation and on resize do nothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `selection` is set when the pin settles (coordinate only) and again when the address arrives. Its coordinate is always where the pin points; the address is the nearest one found. Setting `selection` from outside, a search result or a saved place, moves the map there, and a place that already has an address is shown without a lookup.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The address is looked up 300 ms after the map settles. A new settle, or leaving the screen, cancels the lookup in flight and its request, and an answer for a spot that is no longer under the pin is dropped. Answers are cached per picker by position rounded to about 5 m (the 40 most recent), so nudging back to a known spot sends nothing, which also keeps clear of the geocoder's rate limit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: iOS 26 uses `MKReverseGeocodingRequest`, reading the street and postal code from the map item's placemark (dynamically, as Address Field does) with `MKAddressRepresentations` as the fallback. iOS 17 to 25 uses `CLGeocoder`, kept in a deprecated function that only runs below iOS 26, so the file builds without warnings on both.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The card is a floating liquid glass panel. It has one state per moment: the last address (or "Dropped pin" until one has been found) dimmed with "Locating…" from the moment the map moves until the next address arrives (the "Locating…" line breathes once the pin is down), loading lines only for the first lookup and for Retry, street and locality once found, "Dropped pin" with the coordinates where there is no address (open water), and "Couldn't find the address" with the coordinates when the lookup fails (offline, throttled). Every state keeps the same two lines, and the readout changes once per move: each line morphs letter by letter as the address arrives, so letters the old and new lines share hold still and a nudge along a street moves only the house number (a line too long to fit shrinks to fit and blurs across instead). The card keeps its tallest size and the map's center only moves when it grows, so nothing jumps as the text changes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: When the lookup fails, a glass Retry bubble pinches off the card's trailing end: the card gives up that width and Retry springs out of its end, joined to it by a liquid neck. It melts back into the card when tapped or when the map moves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Confirm is a red glass capsule resting apart below the card. It buds down out of the card once the spot under the pin has its answer (its address, no address, or a failed lookup), born inside the card and pulling a liquid neck that thins and snaps as it springs to its place, and melts back up into the card on a spring with no bounce, its red draining as it goes, the moment the map moves. Its place keeps its height while it is away, so the card and the map's center never move. A Retry keeps it out; tapped while that lookup runs, it spins and waits for the address (up to four seconds), then hands over the place; after a failed lookup it hands over the coordinate alone. Return confirms with a hardware keyboard. Leave out `onConfirm` to hide it and read `selection` yourself.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The locate button asks for When In Use permission on its first tap, never on appear. It spins while finding you, flies the camera to you, and fills in once the pin sits on you; a fix from the last minute is used at once. When your location can't be found it shakes once, on the beat of the error haptic. Camera flights take longer the farther they go: about 0.55 s for a VoiceOver nudge or zoom, up to 1.2 s across town. With approximate location the map shows the area the fix covers instead of a street. When access is denied the arrow is slashed and a tap explains and offers Settings; when it is restricted a tap explains. Dragging works the same without permission.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Where the map starts: the place in `selection`, else `initialCenter`, else the person's location when the app already has permission, else central Lisbon.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: MapKit's logo and legal notice stay visible above the card: the card and Confirm's place inset the map's safe area, which is also where MapKit puts the camera's center.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the address readout is one element, "Selected location", with the address, "Dropped pin" and the coordinates, "Locating" or "Finding the address" as its value. Its actions move the map a quarter of the visible span north, south, east or west, zoom in and out, use your location and retry. After the map settles from a move the new address is announced. The pin is decorative and hidden; the locate button reads its state.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a light tap as the pin meets the ground (at once if the map moves again before it lands, so every settle gets one), success when Confirm hands over the place, a selection tick on Retry, and an error when Retry or locating fails. Nothing while panning, and nothing for a lookup that fails on its own.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the card's text grows and wraps up to accessibility sizes (where it no longer morphs), Retry stays joined to the card's end, Confirm stays full width, and the locate button grows up to 64 pt. Right to left, the card mirrors and the locate button sits top left; the map is never mirrored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Motion: Retry, Confirm and the locate button sink a couple of points under the finger and spring back with a little bounce, and the locate arrow blurs into its filled form, as the spinner and Confirm's label do into each other. The card changes its text in place without moving, and the map's own panning and zooming stay MapKit's. The pin and the map are content and stay as they are; only the chrome over them is glass.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the pin dims instead of lifting and lands without the press, its tap playing as the map settles; the camera jumps instead of flying; Confirm and Retry fade in and out where they rest instead of budding, and the readout cross-fades instead of morphing; the loading lines and "Locating…" still breathe in opacity, so a lookup never looks frozen; buttons shift brightness instead of dipping when pressed; and a failed locate blinks the glyph instead of shaking. Haptics and announcements are unchanged. Reduce Transparency draws the glass solid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The map pans and zooms but doesn't rotate or tilt, so north stays up. A drag that starts on the map pans it, inside a `ScrollView` or a `Form` too; in a sheet, the grabber still dismisses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the glass tint of the card, Retry and the locate button (`surface`, neutral glass by default), label, secondary label, the loading bars (`field`), the pin and its ink, Confirm's tint and its ink, the card's corner radius, points of interest (off by default, so the streets and the pin read first) and the muted map (on by default). `Messages` replaces any line, for example `confirm: "Deliver here"`. `Geocoder` swaps MapKit for your own backend, or a fixed answer for previews and tests.

title: Range Slider
description: A liquid glass dual-thumb slider: two glass bubble thumbs joined by a tinted glass span over a quiet line, with a glass readout chip joined above each thumb on a liquid neck; drag either thumb or touch the track to pull the nearest one over, the thumbs stay under the finger and land on their step when you let go, values snap to a step without floating drift, the thumbs never cross and keep a minimum gap, a thumb pulled past the end of the track gives with rubber-band resistance and springs back, a grabbed thumb swells and its chip takes the span's tint, as the thumbs meet one chip melts into the other to read as one range, and every step ticks a selection haptic with a firmer impact at a bound or the gap.

contents.content: Liquid glass dual-thumb slider that binds a `ClosedRange` of any floating-point type. The thumbs are glass bubbles and the selected span is tinted glass joining them, so the three move as one liquid shape. Each readout chip rests joined above its thumb; when the two would touch, one melts into the other and the survivor reads the whole range. The simplest call is one line: `RangeSlider(value: $price, in: 0...1000, step: 10, format: .currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0)))`. Pass a `FormatStyle` or a `(V) -> String` closure as `format`; it drives the readouts and the VoiceOver values.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Generic over any `BinaryFloatingPoint` (`Double`, `Float`, `CGFloat`). Bind a `ClosedRange`; pass `format:` as a `FormatStyle` (`.currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0))`, `.percent`) or a `(V) -> String` closure. The format drives the readouts and the VoiceOver values.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The slider is one liquid glass shape: the thumbs are clear glass bubbles, and the selected span is tinted glass resting a liquid neck's width from each of them, so it joins them through necks. When the thumbs come close the span gives way and they neck straight into each other. Outside the span the thumbs ride a quiet line that is not glass, so nothing else merges with them.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Drag either thumb, or touch the track and the nearest thumb glides to the finger in one quick move, landing with a little give, while your finger's own movement stays 1:1 on top of it. Grabbing a thumb keeps the finger's offset, so it never jumps under the touch, even while it is still landing from the last release. When both thumbs sit on the same point, the first clear movement decides: right (in left-to-right) takes the upper thumb, left takes the lower.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tracking is never animated: the thumbs follow the finger directly, and only the glide from a track touch and the release spring. Each edge of the span rides its own thumb, so the span stays joined to both through any glide or release. A grabbed thumb lifts: it swells on a quick spring with no overshoot, and drops back with a little give when you let go.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The thumbs never cross. They stop `minimumDistance` apart, kept on the step grid (a 5 gap with step 10 stops at 10). Against the other thumb a thumb stops firm, with no give, and a touch on the track that lands there arrives without overshoot.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Past either end of the track the thumb gives with rubber-band resistance, never more than about its own width (24 to 32pt), while the value stays at the bound. On release it springs back at the speed it was moving. While pulled it draws past the slider's edge, so leave room beside it rather than clipping it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `step` snaps from `bounds.lowerBound`. Both bounds stay reachable when the span is not a multiple of the step (0...1000 by 30 reaches 1000). Values are rounded to the step's decimal places, so `0.1` steps write `0.3`, not `0.30000000000000004`. Out-of-bounds or reversed bindings are shown clamped and written back clean on the first change. While you drag, the value moves step by step and the thumb stays under your finger; when you let go anywhere on the track it snaps onto its step from rest, so its give is a sliver of the distance left and never reaches a neighboring value. Only a thumb pulled past the end keeps its speed as it springs back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Readouts: `.thumbs` (default) rests a glass chip a liquid neck's width above each thumb, joined to it and clamped inside the track. A grabbed thumb's chip takes the span's tint a beat after the thumb lifts. When the two chips would come within 6pt, the right one melts into the left, which widens to read "lower – upper" around the thumbs' midpoint, and it buds back out once they are 12pt apart again, so a thumb resting at the threshold never flickers. `.header` prints "lower – upper" above the track and stacks the values at large text sizes; after a VoiceOver step or an animated change from your code its digits roll without overshoot. `.hidden` shows nothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: `.selection` on each value change while dragging (every 5% of the span without a step), throttled to about 30 per second; a rigid `.impact` once when a thumb reaches a bound or the minimum gap. Nothing plays on press, release or the landing on a step.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Right-to-left: the track mirrors, so the lower thumb sits on the right, and the merged chip reads in the reader's direction.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: two adjustable elements, "Minimum" then "Maximum" (set `lowerLabel` and `upperLabel`, e.g. "Minimum price"). Swipe up or down moves one `step` to the next valid value, or 1% of the span without a step, and the thumb, the span's edge and the chip glide there on the snap spring, landing with the same give as a release.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Thumbs keep a 44pt touch and VoiceOver target even when `Style.thumbSize` draws them smaller. Readouts use text styles and grow with Dynamic Type; all text is semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the line, the span's tint (`fill`, the brand red by default), the thumbs' and chips' glass tints (neutral glass by default), ink, labels, track height and thumb size. `thumbBorder` no longer draws anything: the thumbs are glass bubbles with no ring. `.disabled(true)` desaturates, dims and blocks input.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: a grabbed thumb keeps its size and takes the span's tint instead of swelling, and its chip still fills; the ends of the track stop the thumb without rubber-band give, and glides and landings settle without overshoot. Thumbs follow the finger directly either way. As the chips merge, the right one closes where it is instead of melting across, and the header's digits crossfade instead of rolling. Reduce Transparency draws the glass as solid shapes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The drag starts on touch-down so the track responds to taps; inside a vertical `ScrollView` or sheet, a drag that begins on the slider moves the slider rather than scrolling.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full filter sheet built around it, see the filter sheet in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Scrub Stepper
description: A liquid glass stepper: round minus and plus bubbles joined to a glass numeral pill by liquid necks. Tap, hold to repeat with acceleration, or scrub sideways across the pill for velocity-scaled steps while a ruler slides under the finger; at a bound that button melts into the pill and the pill strains against the stop, and the button buds back out the moment it can be used.

contents.content: Liquid glass minus/plus stepper with hold-to-repeat and a horizontal scrub gesture. The three parts rest joined, so liquid necks hold them together. At a bound the button that can no longer act melts into the numeral pill, and it buds back out of the pill as soon as the value can move that way again. The buttons keep their place in the layout while they are away, so the stepper never changes width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)` covers the whole capsule and decides by start location: the round buttons at each end press, the numeral block in the middle starts a scrub. A press that moves more than 14pt sideways becomes a scrub; one that leaves the capsule by more than 20pt cancels without stepping.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pressed buttons invert (glyph color fills the circle) and sink to 0.86 on a quick spring with no overshoot, then spring back with a little give when you let go; a button at its bound dims. A tap bounces its glyph; a hold or a scrub steps too fast for a bounce to read, so they don't.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hold-to-repeat starts after 400ms and accelerates from 100ms to 60ms after 1.5s and 30ms after 3s. It runs in a `Task` that is cancelled on release, on cancel (including a touch the system takes over), on disappear, and when a bound is hit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Scrubbing consumes one step per 14pt of travel, multiplied by a velocity gain of up to 4x. The value stops when your finger does; nothing coasts. While scrubbing, the block lifts (slightly larger, on a soft shadow) and a ruler fades in a beat later and runs with the finger, faster on a flick. The lift is visual only, so the capsule's layout never changes under the finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Digits roll on a tap, a VoiceOver step or a change from your code, landing without overshoot. While a hold repeats or a scrub steps they change in place, so they stay readable.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every step ticks a `.selection` haptic, throttled to one per 35ms during fast repeats and scrubs. A scrub step that lands on the bound and hits the stop in the same moment fires only the stop's impact.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At a bound, a tap, a repeat tick or a VoiceOver step fires a rigid impact and knocks the block 4pt toward that end and back. A scrub that keeps pushing pulls the block against that end with rubber-band resistance, about 4pt at most, while the ruler stops and the value stays at the bound; the impact fires once each time it reaches the stop, and on release the block springs back at the speed it was moving. The stop holds back no more than 14pt of travel however far you push, so coming back the block relaxes within those 14pt and the value steps one step's travel later.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the trough, buttons, glyph, the numeral block and its ink, and the height (44pt minimum, 52pt by default). `.standard` uses the butter block; pass `.init(block:)` for another.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Supply an `.accessibilityLabel`; the value and adjustable action are provided.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no press scale, no lift scale, no glyph bounce and no block movement at a bound. The buttons still invert, the lifted block keeps its shadow, the ruler still runs, digits cross-fade instead of rolling, a bound darkens the block for a beat instead of moving it, and every haptic stays.

title: Secure Entry
description: A liquid glass password field with a focus ring and a round glass reveal bubble joined to it that keeps focus. Typing buds a strength chip out of the field that morphs its label from weak to strong beside a growing gauge, requirement chips bud out of the field and turn sage with drawn checks as each rule passes, and when all pass the field takes a sage tint with a check while the chips melt back into it; a refused entry shakes the field, tints it butter and buds an error chip joined below it.

contents.content: Liquid glass password field with strength meter, live requirements, and inline error. The field is a glass shape with a round glass reveal bubble joined to it. Everything below it buds out of the field when it appears and melts back into it when it goes: the error chip, joined just under it, and, apart from it, the strength chip and the requirement chips.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The field is liquid glass, with a round glass reveal bubble joined to its end by a liquid neck. Revealing swaps `SecureField` for `TextField` instantly; the toggle re-targets `@FocusState` to the new field so the keyboard stays up, and its eye glyph blurs into the other. The bubble sinks under the finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Focus draws a 2pt ring around the field. The field's glass carries its state: `Style.error` (butter) while there is an error, `Style.success` (sage) once every requirement passes, neutral otherwise. Text on a tinted field turns to dark ink.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Everything below the field lines up with it and buds straight down out of it when it appears, then melts back into it when it goes, while the room it takes opens and closes on the same springs, so whatever sits below moves with it instead of jumping.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Setting `error` from `nil` shakes the field once with an `.error` haptic on the same beat, tints it butter, and buds a butter error chip out of its bottom edge to rest joined just under it. A new message for an error already showing blurs into the new wording in place, with no second shake or haptic, so live validation never buzzes per keystroke. To signal a later refusal, set `error` to `nil` when the user edits, so the next refused submit arrives from `nil` and shakes again. Clearing it melts the chip back into the field as the tint drains.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The strength chip buds out of the field as typing starts and rests apart below it, beside a gauge that fades in. Its label morphs letter by letter from WEAK through FAIR and GOOD to STRONG, and the chip and gauge take the level's tint: butter while weak or fair, sage once good. The gauge changes length without overshoot, so the reading never wobbles.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Requirement chips bud out of the field while it is focused or filled, two to a row, resting apart. A met requirement clicks into sage glass with a small dip and swell, its check drawing in after the tint lands, with a `.selection` haptic. When all four pass, the field turns sage and a check blurs into it with a `.success` haptic in place of the tick and the pop of the last chip, and the chips stay a beat so the last one lands, then melt back into the field. Leaving the field melts them at once, and losing a rule during that beat keeps them.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets every tint plus the field height (also the reveal bubble's diameter) and radius. All text is semibold. `.disabled(true)` dims the field.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no shake and no press scale (the reveal bubble shades instead), the chips open and close where they rest instead of budding, the morphing label and the swapped glyphs crossfade, and met chips change tint without the pop. The tints, the drawn checks and every haptic remain. Reduce Transparency draws the glass as solid shapes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For one-time codes after sign-in, see the Verify screen (code entry) in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Signature Pad
description: A signature field that lays smooth, velocity-weighted ink into a Canvas as the finger moves, thinning on quick flicks and pooling on slow turns, over a baseline whose Sign here hint fades on the first stroke. Under the paper floats one liquid glass toolbar: Undo buds out of one end of the Type instead pill and Clear out of the other the moment they can act, joined to it by liquid necks, and melt back into it when they can't; the pill morphs to Draw instead, and a sage glass Signed chip lands once the signature counts. Undo after Clear, strokes that rescale with the pad on rotation, and export to a transparent PNG or a vector PDF.

contents.content: Signature capture that feels like ink, bound to a `SignaturePad.Signature` value you own. Strokes are smoothed through midpoint quadratics and weighted by speed (fast strokes run thin, slow turns run full), drawn in a `Canvas` one layer per stroke so finished strokes never redraw while you sign. Points are stored in the pad's coordinate space together with the pad size they were captured at, so the signature rescales with the pad on rotation and exports at any size. A drag that starts in the pad draws and never scrolls an enclosing `ScrollView`; a drag that starts outside still scrolls. `swift @State private var signature = SignaturePad.Signature() SignaturePad(signature: $signature) Button("Confirm delivery") { upload(signature.pngData(size: CGSize(width: 600, height: 200))) } .disabled(signature.isEmpty) `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Ink is weighted by speed, the way a pen behaves: each sample's width falls from `Style.lineWidth` toward about half of it as the finger speeds up, eased over 35 ms so strokes swell and thin smoothly. The line runs through the midpoints of the touch samples as quadratic curves, cut into short pieces whose widths interpolate, so there are no corners or width steps, and long gaps from very fast strokes are bridged by the same curves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each stroke is its own `Canvas` layer, grouped into a few paths by width. Finished strokes never redraw while you sign, so long signatures stay smooth.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A tap draws a dot. `isEmpty` stays `true` until there is at least `Signature.minimumInk` of ink (12% of the pad width, about 40pt on a phone) or a typed name, so a stray tap or speck never enables your submit button. `strokes.isEmpty` tells you whether anything is on the pad at all, and `inkLength` lets you set a stricter rule.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Points are stored in the pad's coordinates together with the pad size they were captured at (`canvasSize`). When the pad changes size (rotation, split view, a different `Style.height`) the signature scales uniformly, anchored to the bottom and the leading edge so it stays on the line next to the cross. Strokes added after a resize join the same space.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Undo removes the last stroke with a short fade and a rigid tick. Clear fades out the whole signature at once with a medium tick, and Undo right after Clear fades it all back in, until anything else changes. A soft tick marks the first touch of each stroke. With a hardware keyboard, Command-Z undoes and Command-Delete clears.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The ink itself is never animated: each stroke draws under the finger as it moves and stays exactly as drawn when the finger lifts, so the export matches the screen. Only the chrome around it moves, and quietly.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The "Sign here" hint fades and drops a few points on the first touch, and settles back in when the pad is empty again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Once the signature counts and the pad has been still for a moment, a small sage glass Signed chip pops in at the far end of the status line under the baseline, where the hint sat, with a bounce and a success tap, the first time for each signature. When it comes back after a later pause it lands with just a little give and no tap, so a signature written in parts doesn't celebrate on every pause. Ink and a typed name arm apart: the tap re-arms once the ink no longer counts or the name is blank, so Type instead and back never replays it for the same strokes, and a draft passed in already signed doesn't tap on appear. It steps out quickly when the finger comes back, and a stroke that starts under it still draws.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The toolbar is one liquid glass shape floating centred under the paper, on the page rather than on the paper, where clear glass would all but vanish. Type instead is the pill in the middle; Undo (a round bubble) rests joined to its leading end and Clear (a capsule) to its trailing end, so liquid necks hold the three together and they read as one control. Each bubble is there only while it can act. The moment there is something to take back or clear, it buds out of its end of the pill, born inside it and springing to its place; when there is nothing left to undo or clear it melts back into the pill on a spring with no bounce, its label going first. Clear melts home after Clear, while Undo stays out to bring the signature back. Both side slots keep their width while a bubble is away, so the pill never moves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The bubbles sink about 1.5 pt a side under the finger and spring back with a little bounce, and their labels dim while pressed. Glass is neutral; `Style.control` tints it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A drag that starts in the pad draws from the first touch and never scrolls an enclosing `ScrollView` or `Form`; a drag that starts outside the pad scrolls as usual. If the system cancels a touch (a call, a presented sheet), the stroke so far is kept.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Type instead turns the line into a text field set in a script face (Snell Roundhand, a system font, so nothing is bundled). The pill's label morphs letter by letter to Draw instead and its glyph blurs from the keyboard to the signature; Undo melts home, since typing has nothing to undo, and Clear buds back out beside the pill once there is a name to clear. The ink fades out first and the field follows a beat behind, so strokes and the name barely overlap; the field takes focus and the keyboard rises at once. Draw instead brings the ink back with a short, firm fade, at full strength about 0.3 s after the tap. The name sits on the same baseline and shrinks to fit when it is long. Scripts the face lacks fall back to the system font. Drawn strokes are kept while typing, so Draw instead brings them back; while `typedName` is non-nil it is the signature for `isEmpty` and export.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Export: `image(size:scale:ink:lineWidth:trimmed:)` and `pngData` give a transparent PNG, and `pdfData` gives a one-page vector PDF. `trimmed` (the default) crops to the ink so the signature fills the image; `false` keeps the whole pad area with the signature where it sat. Ink defaults to black, whatever the on-screen appearance. A typed signature exports in the same script face. Both can be called off the main actor.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Signature` is `Codable` and `Equatable`, so a draft can be saved and restored, and `.onChange(of:)` sees every stroke.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the pad reads "Signature" with a value of Empty, Too short to count as a signature, or Signed. Double-tapping lets a VoiceOver user draw directly on it (direct touch), and the pad offers Type your name instead, Undo and Clear as actions. Undo, Clear and restores are announced. The typed field reads "Signature, typed name".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the hint and the Signed chip fade without moving, Undo and Clear fade in and out where they rest instead of budding, the mode label cross-fades instead of morphing, and the controls shift brightness instead of sinking (their labels still dim). Reduce Transparency draws the glass solid. Strokes and mode switches are fades either way; the mode hand-off becomes a quick crossfade. Haptics and announcements are unchanged.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the toolbar controls scale, and Undo and Clear move to a second row under Type instead when they no longer fit on one line; they bud down out of the middle of the pill there. The hint grows up to accessibility sizes and shrinks to fit under the line; the cross and baseline keep a fixed position so they stay aligned with stored strokes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `allowsTyping: false` removes Type instead. It is the accessible path for people who cannot draw a signature, so turn it off only when your flow offers another way to sign.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the pad, ink, label and secondary colors, the glass tint of the toolbar bubbles (`control`, neutral by default) and of the Signed chip (`signed`), ink weight, corner radius and the paper's height (`nil` fills the height offered, for a full-screen signing sheet). `.disabled(true)` dims the pad and stops drawing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: **v1.2:** the pad is one card. Type instead sits at the leading end of a toolbar along the top, Undo and Clear at the trailing end, and a hairline separates the toolbar from the drawing area. Ink is clipped to the drawing area, so a stroke carried up past the hairline never draws over the controls. Under the baseline is a status line: the hint while the pad is empty, the Signed chip at its far end once the signature counts.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: **v1.3:** heavier ink. `lineWidth` defaults to 5pt (was 3.6) for drawing and for `image`, `pngData` and `pdfData`, and fast strokes thin to about half the width instead of about 40%, so a quick signature still reads as a confident pen line.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: **v1.4:** liquid glass. Type instead, Undo and Clear are glass bubbles in one cluster at the leading end of the toolbar; Undo and Clear bud out of Type instead when they can act and melt back into it when they can't, instead of dimming. The Signed chip is sage glass. All text and symbols are semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: **v1.5:** the paper is the whole card, with a hairline edge and a soft lift, and no toolbar strip inside it. The toolbar floats centred under the paper as one liquid shape: Undo buds out of the Type instead pill's leading end and Clear out of its trailing end, resting joined to it, so the necks hold.

Drawn strokes, or a typed name when the person chose Type instead. `isEmpty` stays `true` until there is a typed name or enough ink to count (a stray dot or speck does not), so it is the right check for enabling a submit button. Setting it from outside redraws the pad; a stroke removed from outside inside `withAnimation` fades out.

title: Token Field
description: A liquid glass tag and recipient field where each committed entry buds out of the glass input as a glass chip, born where it was typed while the input slides on, and chips wrap across lines resting apart while the input takes the rest of the last line. Return, comma or a paste of a whole list commits trimmed tokens with duplicate, limit and validation checks; backspace on an empty input highlights the last chip in the brand red and a second press melts it back into the input; and a glass suggestion list buds out of the input and filters as you type.

contents.content: Wrapping liquid glass token entry bound to an array of strings: tags, skills, recipients. The input is a glass capsule and every token a glass chip beside it, resting apart. A committed token buds out of the input where it was typed; a removed one melts back into it. Suggestions bud out of the input as a glass list.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The input is a liquid glass capsule and every token a glass chip beside it. They sit in a private wrapping `Layout`: leading-aligned rows that rest apart, outside the distance at which glass melts together, with the input taking the rest of the last line. When that is narrower than the input's minimum (88pt, scaled) or its typed text, the input wraps to a new full-width line, and grows taller as wrapped text needs. A chip wider than the field truncates in the middle.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Return, comma (including the full-width `，` and `、`) and pasted line breaks commit the trimmed text by default. `separators` adds `.semicolon` and `.space` for recipient lists. Pasting `a, b, c` adds three tokens in one animated change.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A committed token buds out of the input as a glass chip: it is born inside the input, under the text it was typed as, and springs out to its place while the input slides on to make room, the neck between them stretching until it snaps. Several tokens from one paste bud out one after another. The reflowing chips and the input move on a short spring with a little give; on a field wider than 400pt (landscape, iPad), where a wrap travels most of the line, they move without overshoot so nothing crosses the field's edge. Chips added from outside bud out of the input's leading end the same way.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every entry is checked in order: `maxTokens`, then duplicates (case-insensitive, the first spelling is kept), then `validate`. Entries refused by `validate` or past the limit stay in the input so they can be fixed: the field shakes once, the input takes the `Style.error` tint (butter) and an `.error` haptic plays on the same beat. A duplicate leaves the input and points at the chip already there instead: that chip lifts into its highlight and swells once with the `.error` haptic, every time, even when it is already highlighted, and the field stays still. The swell takes only the room the lift leaves before the next chip; one too long to swell at all dims for a beat instead. Each commit plays one haptic: `.selection` when everything was added, `.error` when anything was refused, even if other parts of the paste were added.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Backspace on an empty input highlights the last chip with a soft impact: it takes the `Style.selection` tint, the brand red, and lifts 4% on a short spring. A second backspace removes it with a rigid impact: the chip leaves the flow at once, so its neighbors and the input reflow into its place, and it melts back into the input from where it was, its tint draining as it goes. Tapping a chip highlights it the same way. The remove glyph on each chip sinks slightly under the finger and springs back with a little bounce. A zero-width space kept in front of the typed text makes this reliable on the software keyboard, where iOS reports no key event for backspace on an empty field. It is never shown or committed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The input uses a vertical-axis `TextField`, so return inserts a line break the field turns into a commit and the keyboard stays up between tokens. Valid text left in the input is committed quietly, with no haptic, when the field loses focus.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Suggestions appear while typing, matched case- and diacritic-insensitively, prefix matches first, at most five, with the matched run in full ink and the rest quieter. Tokens already added are left out. The list is a glass panel that buds out of the input, shrunk inside it, and rests apart below the field, opening room for itself as it comes and closing it as it melts home, so whatever sits below moves with it. While you type its rows refine in place on a short spring with no overshoot, so the text you read never wobbles, and a row sinks slightly under the finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style.chips` tints chips by their text, so a token keeps its tint wherever it appears and removing one never recolors the rest; the house palette leaves every chip neutral glass. A tinted chip's suggestion row shows a dot in its tint.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At `maxTokens` the input stops accepting text and shows a quiet count such as `5/5`. A keystroke there meets a bound rather than an error: a light impact, and the count swells and rebounds, with no shake or error haptic on every key. While the input still holds text, such as entries kept past the limit, the count is hidden, so the ring dims for a beat instead. Backspace still removes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Typing never waits on motion. An edit never animates the input or its text, even when it changes the suggestions, clears the error tint or wraps the input to a new line; only a commit or a removal moves the input, along with the chips.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tapping anywhere in the field that is not a chip focuses the input. Keyboard type, capitalization and content type pass through: apply `.keyboardType(.emailAddress)` and friends to the `TokenField`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each chip is one element read as "Swift, token" with a Remove action; the input's label carries the placeholder and the token count; adds, removals and rejections are announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the input's and list's glass tint, chip tints, ink, label, placeholder, the error and selection tints, the list's corner radius and the field's minimum height. All text is semibold. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and disables removal.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: chips and the suggestion list open and close where they rest instead of budding and melting, and chips reflow on a short spring with no bounce. A highlighted chip changes tint without lifting, and a duplicate dims its chip for a beat instead of swelling it. A refused entry plays its haptic and dims the ring for a beat instead of shaking, so a refusal while the error tint is already showing still shows on screen. A keystroke at the limit dims the count for a beat instead of swelling it, or the ring while the input holds text, as with motion on. A pressed remove glyph or suggestion row fades instead of sinking. Reduce Transparency draws the glass as solid shapes.

title: Depth Carousel
description: Paged cards that recede in depth as they leave center and hand each page a phase value for inner parallax. A held neighbor starts forward and comes to center on tap. Underneath, a glass page counter joined by a liquid neck to a scrubbable glass track, whose tinted glass pill stretches between the dots as the pages move, flattens against the ends and follows the finger when scrubbed, computed in absolute page coordinates so it never jumps.

contents.content: Centered paging carousel with depth recession, per-page parallax phase, and a progress-linked indicator.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Snapping uses `.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)` with content margins sized so the aligned page is centered; the first and last pages center too. Fractional progress is read from the page row's position in a coordinate space named on the scroll view itself (the built-in `.scrollView` space starts inside the content margins), so it lands on whole pages and works on iOS 17 without `onScrollGeometryChange`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Depth is driven by the same progress: pages shrink by `style.recede`, fade by `style.dim`, and their shadow gets lighter and leans back toward the centered page as they leave center. The `phase` handed to your content is -1...1, for inner parallax; the example drifts a cropped ink disc by `phase * 40` inside a solid color card. Under Reduce Motion the phase is 0 and only the dim remains.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hold a neighbor page and it starts forward, about a third of the way to center; tap it and it comes the rest of the way on the snap spring that every tap, scrub and VoiceOver page move uses. A swipe that starts on a neighbor scrolls as usual and cancels the press. The centered page keeps its own gestures.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The pages stay your content; the indicator under them is liquid glass. A "01 / 04" counter (current page in rounded semibold, total dimmed, with a short roll and no overshoot as it changes) sits on a glass capsule joined by a liquid neck to the glass track that carries the dots, so the two read as one control, centered under the pages. The current page is a pill of tinted glass (`style.indicatorActive`) riding inside the track. It is drawn in absolute page coordinates, as a pure function of the scroll position, so it never lags the pages and never jumps when one settles. Between two dots its leading edge reaches the next dot first and its trailing edge follows, so it stretches by up to half the dot spacing and gathers in as the page lands. Past the first or last page it flattens against the end dot as the scroll view rubber-bands, and springs back with it. On iOS 26 this is Liquid Glass; before that frosted Material, and under Reduce Transparency solid fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While you drag the pages or touch the track, the dots dim and the pill widens, on one press spring. They settle back on the snap spring as soon as you let go of the track, or once dragged pages come to rest, so after a fling they stay active until the pages land. The whole 44pt-tall track is scrubbable: the pill glides onto the finger in about 0.1s while following its movement 1:1, flattening against the ends if you pull past them, while the pages follow on the snap spring, with a selection haptic per page. On release the pill eases back to the page position; touch the track again before it gets there and it is picked up from where it is drawn, without a jump.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`DepthCarousel.Style`, also `DepthCarouselStyle`): `recede`, `dim`, `shadowOpacity`, `indicatorActive`, `indicatorInactive`, `showsCounter`. With `showsCounter` off the track stands alone.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: pages don't scale or hand out a phase, and keep their dim. The pill slides rigidly without stretching, stops at the ends and doesn't widen; the dots still dim. A held neighbor shades slightly (darker in light mode, lighter in dark) instead of moving forward. The counter fades instead of rolling, and page moves land on a short spring with no overshoot. Native paging and its fling are unchanged.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver treats the carousel as one container that reads "Page x of y" and supports swipe up/down to change pages; the indicator is hidden from it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `scrollClipDisabled()` lets neighbor pages peek past the carousel's own bounds, so give it full width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Want blur-and-tone depth, pinch peek-zoom and a full album screen? That is the Depth Gallery screen in SwiftPieces Pro.
