title: Drag Select Grid
description: A multi-select photo and file grid where one drag paints a whole reading-order range the way the system photo library does, a sideways drag or a short hold starts painting while vertical swipes still scroll, dragging back unpaints, starting on a selected item deselects, the grid auto-scrolls faster the deeper the finger sits in the top or bottom edge, and selected cells inset under a liquid glass badge that buds out of the print's corner, floods signal red as the check stamps down and melts back into the corner, with a haptic tick per item.

contents.content: A scrolling grid of `Identifiable` items with drag-to-select: photos, files, attachments, media. In selection mode a sideways drag (or a short hold, then any direction) paints every item from the first one touched to the one under the finger, in reading order. Dragging back unpaints. Starting on a selected item deselects instead. A vertical swipe still scrolls, and holding the finger near the top or bottom edge scrolls the grid while painting. Tap toggles one item.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: In selection mode, a drag that starts mostly sideways (within about 40 degrees of horizontal) paints. So does a short hold (0.25s) followed by a drag in any direction, which is how you paint straight down a column. Anything steeper than 40 degrees without a hold scrolls, the same as any grid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Painting covers the reading-order range from the first item touched to the one under the finger, like the system photo library. Dragging back shrinks the range and each item returns to what it was before the drag. Starting on a selected item deselects the range instead.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hold the finger in the top or bottom band (72pt by default) and the grid auto-scrolls while you paint. Speed grows linearly with depth into the band, up to 1200pt a second at the edge, and rows scrolled into view keep painting under a still finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A tap toggles one item. Outside selection mode taps reach your cell content (buttons, links), and with `longPressToSelect` a 0.45s hold turns selection mode on, selects that item and keeps painting. Pass `false` if your cells have their own context menu.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A hold shows itself building: once the finger has rested 0.1s, the print under it sinks a couple of points, and when the hold fires the selection takes over from there. A quick scroll moves past the 8pt decision before then and never dips a cell. A scroll that starts after a pause, a lift or a cancelled touch lets the print back up at once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The gesture is a small UIKit recognizer the grid installs on its own scroll view. It decides between painting and scrolling within the first 8 points of movement, and the grid's scroll view (and any scroll view around it, such as a screen-level `ScrollView`) waits for that decision, so a paint never scrolls and a scroll never paints.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Columns are as many as fit at `minimumCellWidth`, so the grid adapts to rotation, iPad and split view. Selection is kept by ID across column changes. Items are hit-tested from the grid's geometry, not from cell frames, so painting works through rows a lazy grid has not built yet.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: When items disappear, their IDs drop out of `selection`, and a drag in progress ends. Turning `isSelecting` off keeps `selection`; clear it yourself if your design does.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Selected cells inset (`selectedScale`, 0.86) under a liquid glass badge in the bottom trailing corner. In selection mode every print shows the badge as clear glass with a light rim, so it is clear it can be picked; picked, it floods the house signal red with a dark check, so a picked print reads at a glance on any thumbnail. Each badge is its own glass bubble, a cell apart from the next. The badge scales with Dynamic Type up to 34pt, and never past a third of the cell.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Selecting is a press then a stamp: the print presses into its slot on a firm spring with a small give as its badge floods red, and a beat later the check comes down onto the badge and lands with a visible bounce. Deselecting lifts the check off quickly, drains the tint and lets the print back out with only a slight give, so dragging back across a range reads as a soft release. Your cell content changes on the same spring as the inset. Painting never waits on any of this: the selection changes the moment the finger reaches an item.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Badges bud out of their print's corner: each is born just past the corner, shrunk and hidden by the print's rounded clip, and springs out to its place. When a long press turns selection mode on, they spread out from the held print, one row or column per beat, all within about 120ms. Turned on from your own control, they bud together. Leaving selection mode, the badges of unpicked prints melt back into their corners together, on a spring with no bounce.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact when a paint starts, a selection tick per item crossed (at most about 22 a second, so fast drags and auto-scroll do not buzz), and a selection tick on tap.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each cell is one element with your content's label and the selected trait. In selection mode it is a button that toggles on double-tap. Every cell has a Select or Deselect action, and Select also turns selection mode on, so everything painting does is reachable without it. After a paint, the new count is announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Right-to-left layouts mirror the grid; painting follows the mirrored reading order.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the inset and the badge tint change on a short spring with no overshoot, the check fades in place instead of stamping, the badges fade in and out in place together instead of budding, and a held print dims instead of sinking. Reduce Transparency draws the badges as solid shapes. Auto-scroll still runs, since it is driven by the finger, and every haptic still plays.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.disabled(true)` turns off painting, taps and the hold. `Style` sets spacing, corner radius, the selected inset, badge, check and ring colors, the auto-scroll band and speed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The example is a small library of flat scenes in the house blocks (hills, a sunset, portraits, a night sky, an arch, fields), drawn in a `Canvas` so they read as photos, with a liquid glass toolbar under the grid: a signal Done (Select outside selection mode) and the live count, which buds out of Done with the first pick, joined to it, and melts back in when the selection empties. Done also clears the selection there.

title: Follow Scroll
description: A chat, log and live-feed scroll container that opens on the newest item and stays pinned to it while the reader is at the bottom, but never yanks them away once they scroll up to read; items that arrive below are counted into a liquid glass pill that buds up out of the bottom edge on a neck, jumps back to the latest and melts back down into the edge once the reader is caught up, older items loaded at the top keep the visible row exactly where it was while a glass spinner buds down from the top edge, and keyboard, rotation, growing rows and removals all hold the reader's place.

contents.content: Colors and metrics for `FollowScroll`. `.standard` is the house palette.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Opens on the newest item and, while the reader is within `followThreshold` (48pt) of the bottom, scrolls each new item into view with a short smooth scroll. Many items arriving in one update scroll once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Once the reader scrolls up, new items never move the content. They are counted into a liquid glass pill at the bottom, such as "3 new", with a red dot and a down arrow. Tapping it (or ⌘↓ on a hardware keyboard) jumps to the latest and clears the count; scrolling back down by hand clears it too. Items removed before they are seen drop out of the count.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The pill buds out of the scroll view's bottom edge, the edge the rows slip under (the screen's bottom, or the top of a composer). Just past that edge lies a hidden glass lip: the pill is born inside it, rises through the edge pulling a liquid neck that snaps just clear of it, and settles with a small give above the safe area. When the reader is caught up it melts back down into the edge on a spring with no bounce, keeping the count it had, its label blurring away first so nothing rides it down. Each new count rolls the number and eases the pill's width without overshoot, so a busy feed never keeps it wobbling and the count never shows a number that isn't true.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: More than three quarters of a screen above the latest with nothing new, the pill shows as a compact round jump button, and it stays until the reader is back within about 60% of a screen, so it never flickers at the line. When news arrives it changes form rather than being swapped, with a slight give: the same arrow slides over as the red dot grows in just behind it, and the count opens beside it. Turn it off with `Style(showsJumpButton: false)`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `alwaysFollow` jumps to the bottom for chosen items even when scrolled up. Pass `\.isMine` so the reader's own sent message always comes into view.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `onReachTop` loads older items when the reader nears the top (within about three quarters of a screen). Prepend them to `items` before it returns: the rows on screen stay exactly where they are, including when the reader is resting on the very top edge. A small glass bubble with a spinner buds down out of the top edge while it runs and melts back up into it when it is done. It never runs twice at once, it runs again while a short list still reaches the top, and a call that adds nothing is not repeated until the reader scrolls away and back, so an exhausted history or a failed request never loops.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Stays pinned to the bottom when the container changes size while following: the keyboard (for a composer in `safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)`), rotation, or the last row growing as text streams into it. Scrolled up, the reader's place holds through all of these.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Replacing the whole array (another conversation, a new filter) starts again at the latest with the count cleared. Removing the newest items is not treated as a reset.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Only a scroll by the reader leaves the bottom: rows inserted above, lazy rows re-measuring and resizes never do. On iOS 18 and later a finger on the content also holds back any automatic scroll until the gesture ends.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isFollowing` (optional binding) reflects whether the view is pinned, for a "Live" badge or a toolbar button; set it to `true` to jump to the latest.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `empty` is shown centered while there are no items. Rows are laid out in a `LazyVStack`, so long threads and logs stay cheap.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tracking: iOS 18 and later read `onScrollGeometryChange` and `onScrollPhaseChange`; iOS 17 measures the content in the scroll view's coordinate space. Both feed the same logic, and position is held through `scrollPosition(id:anchor:)` on the bottom-most row.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pill and spinner: Liquid Glass on iOS 26 (interactive on the pill), a frosted material with a light rim and a soft shadow earlier, and the solid `Style.surface` under Reduce Transparency. All text and glyphs are semibold. On iOS 26 the interactive glass gives the press; elsewhere the pill sinks slightly under the finger and springs back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the pill is a button read as its label ("3 new") with the hint "Jump to latest"; the scroll view offers a "Jump to latest" action while scrolled up; new items that arrive while scrolled up are announced once per burst with the final count.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Localization: `newItemLabel` gives the pill text and the announcement. The default is a localized "3 new" through `String(localized:)`; add plural variants in your String Catalog, or pass your own. The pill mirrors in right-to-left layouts.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the pill and its dot scale, the label wraps to two lines at the largest sizes, and the hit area never drops below 44pt.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: jumps are instant instead of scrolling, the pill and the spinner fade in and out in place instead of budding and melting, the red dot fades instead of growing and the arrow keeps its size, the count crossfades instead of rolling, and where the pill is not Liquid Glass a press dims it instead of sinking it. In either mode rows never pick up an animation, and the corrections that keep the bottom glued (keyboard, rotation, a growing row) and the prepend restore are instant.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a light tap when the pill first appears with news, and a soft one when you jump. Nothing fires for each new item.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the pill's label, signal dot and ink, the Reduce Transparency surface, the spinner color, row spacing, horizontal and vertical padding, the follow threshold and whether the compact jump button shows.

title: Paged List
description: An async/await infinite-scroll list that prefetches the next page a few rows before the end, never runs two loads at once, drops duplicate ids across pages, ignores stale responses after a refresh or cancel, and shows pulsing skeleton rows; its footer is one liquid glass bubble that spins while a page loads, widens into a "Couldn't load more" pill with a Retry bubble budding out of it on a liquid neck that keeps loaded rows, and becomes a quiet "You're all caught up" pill at the end, with pull to refresh that replaces rows only on success.

contents.content: An infinitely scrolling list driven by an async page loader, with every pagination state handled. The simplest call is one line: `PagedList(load: api.page) { item in Row(item) }`, or for page-number APIs `PagedList(pageSize: 20) { page in try await api.fetch(page: page) } row: { item in Row(item) }`. To restart with new parameters (a search query, a filter), give the list `.id(query)`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `load` receives `nil` for the first page, then each page's `next` cursor, which can be a page number, an offset or an opaque token. Return `PagedListPage(items:next:)` with `next: nil` on the last page. For page-number APIs, `PagedList(pageSize:)` builds the cursor for you and ends the list at the first short or empty page.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The next page starts when the row `prefetchDistance` (5) rows from the end appears, or when the footer is on screen, so short pages keep loading until the screen fills. Only one load runs at a time; extra triggers are ignored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Items whose `id` has already been seen are dropped, so an API that shifts under you (new items pushing old ones into the next page) never produces duplicate rows. Eight pages in a row that add nothing new end the list, to guard against a cursor that never ends.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every load takes a generation number. A refresh, a retry or leaving the screen cancels the load in flight and starts a new generation, and any response from an older one is dropped, so a slow page can never overwrite fresher rows. A load cancelled by disappearing resumes when the list appears again. Throwing `CancellationError` or `URLError.cancelled` is never shown as an error.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: States: skeleton rows while the first page loads, with a pulse that travels down them a beat apart (pass `placeholder:` to render your own row redacted instead), and a footer that is one liquid glass bubble: it spins while more loads, widens into a "Couldn't load more" pill with a butter warning disc and a signal Retry bubble that keeps every loaded row, and becomes a quiet "You're all caught up" pill with a sage check at the end (`endMessage: nil` hides it). If the first page fails, a full error view shows a butter glass warning bubble and a signal glass Try again button.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Motion stays out of the data's way: the first page, page appends and refresh replacements are never animated. Only the status around them moves. The footer changes form about its centre on a spring with a slight give, its glyph and label blurring from one state to the next. On a failure the Retry bubble buds out of the pill's trailing end, held to it by a liquid neck, and when Retry is tapped it melts back in, its tint draining, as the pill folds back to the spinner. The error and empty views fade in and out over the list. On iOS 26 Retry and Try again are interactive glass; elsewhere they sink a few points when pressed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Empty: the built-in state is a short message. Pass `empty:` for your own view, for example `ContentUnavailableView("No receipts", systemImage: "doc.text")`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pull to refresh reloads from the first page and replaces the rows only when it succeeds. If it fails, the old rows stay and a "Couldn't refresh" pill appears above them, and its Retry bubble buds out of it. With `layout: .plain` the pill eases in; a `List` inserts it without animation, so no row slides under a pull that is still held. While a refresh runs, a spinner stands in for Retry's arrow and Retry ignores taps, so it can't restart the refresh it is waiting on; if it fails again, the warning disc gives one short shake.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `layout: .list` (default) is a plain `List`, so swipe actions and row modifiers work in your row. `layout: .plain` uses a `LazyVStack` in a `ScrollView` with `Style.rowSpacing` and `Style.contentPadding`. Appending pages never moves the scroll position in either.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: To restart with new parameters, such as a search query or filter, give the list `.id(query)`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Concurrency: state lives on the main actor; `load` is a `@Sendable` async closure that runs off it. Items must be `Identifiable & Sendable`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`PagedListStyle`): `text`, `secondaryText`, `field`, `error`, `retry`, `end`, `ink`, `rowSpacing`, `contentPadding`, `skeletonRows`. Colour follows meaning: `error` (butter) marks warnings, `retry` (signal red) tints the primary action, `end` (sage) marks success, and the pill itself is neutral glass (`field` under Reduce Transparency). The pill, discs and Retry scale with Dynamic Type, and at accessibility sizes Retry buds out below the pill instead of beside it. All text is semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: "Loaded 20 more" is announced when a page appends, and each error is announced. The skeleton reads as a single "Loading" element, the spinner as "Loading more", and Retry is a button with a hint, read as "Retrying" and dimmed while a refresh runs.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the skeleton rows breathe together instead of the pulse travelling down them, the spinner becomes three fading dots, Retry fades in and out in place instead of budding and melting, glyphs and labels crossfade, the refresh pill fades instead of scaling, Retry dims instead of sinking when pressed where it is not Liquid Glass, and the disc doesn't shake. Reduce Transparency draws the glass as solid shapes. A light haptic plays on Retry; routine loads are silent.

title: Status Timeline
description: A vertical status timeline on liquid glass nodes: the live node is tinted and breathes, completed ones stamp to a tinted check as the ink runs down the line to the next stop, and a step's detail buds out of its node as a glass panel joined to it, melting back in as the relay moves on.

contents.content: Vertical timeline for order tracking, delivery, or verification flows. Each step's node is a liquid glass bubble, tinted by its status. An open step's detail sits on a glass panel that buds out of its node and rests joined to it by a liquid neck, so the node and its detail read as one shape.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every node is a liquid glass bubble, tinted by its status: the live step signal (`style.current`) with a breathing ring, completed steps sage with a drawn check, a failed step butter with an x, and pending steps clear glass with a quiet number. On iOS 26 this is Liquid Glass; before that frosted Material, and under Reduce Transparency solid fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: An open step's detail sits on a glass panel that buds out of its node: born inside the node as a small round blob, it grows out into the panel behind the step's text and rests joined to the node by a liquid neck, so the node and its detail read as one shape. The live step's panel takes the signal tint with dark ink, a failed step's the butter tint, any other step's stays clear glass. Closing, the detail blurs away, the panel's tint drains and it melts back into the node.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Layout is nodes leading, content trailing: a 44pt column holds the 30pt node and the connector below it, which stretches to the row's own height, so long titles and expanded detail never break the line. Rows hug their content, so the timeline never stretches to fill a tall container. Each row's glass is its own liquid group, so a node holds its own panel and never melts into its neighbour.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A status change plays as a relay down the trail. The step that completes stamps first: its number blurs out, its node takes the sage tint, the check draws a beat later, and as it lands the node pops with the `.success` haptic. Its open panel drains and melts back into the node. The ink then runs down its connector in the text color, on a fixed 0.4s clock, and the next step takes its new status only as the ink reaches it: its node lights signal, and with `expandsCurrent` its panel buds out a beat after that.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A `.failed` step lands the same way: its node turns butter with an x, gives a small shake with the `.error` haptic on the same beat, and the connector below it turns dashed, so the trail visibly stops. A reset or any change that doesn't complete a step lands in one beat, with checks and ink clearing quickly.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A change that completes three or more steps at once is catching up rather than handing off, so it lands in one beat. Steps are tracked by title: a step that moves still relays its change, a renamed one shows its status at once, and a repeated title keeps its own state. A newer change mid-relay carries on from what is on screen, and a stamp it cuts short still plays its haptic once. Each change plays each haptic once. A timeline that appears shows its current state without replaying anything, its open panel already out, and one that changed while off screen catches up as it returns, its tints, checks and ink settling together with no relay and no haptics. VoiceOver reads every step's real status at once, never the relay's delayed drawing of it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tap any step with `detail` to expand it; one step is expanded at a time. The row grows around the detail on a calm spring while the panel buds out and the text blurs in, clipped to the panel so it never shows past its edge; closing is quicker. `expandsCurrent` opens the current step on appearance and follows it as the live step moves on, including a move made while the timeline was off screen, which it shows as it stands on return.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`StatusTimeline.Style`): `current`, `complete`, `failed`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`. `surface` is kept so existing code compiles but no longer draws anything: open detail sits on glass. `tint:` still overrides both the current and complete colors.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under Reduce Motion every change lands in one short beat with no relay: tints, checks, ink and detail crossfade without drawing, popping or shaking, panels fade in place instead of budding, and the rows reflow once. The breathing ring becomes a still halo that breathes in opacity, so the live step still reads as in progress. The colors, the marks and both haptics still carry each change. Each step is a single VoiceOver element that reads its title, timestamp and status, and is a button only when it has detail.

title: Swipe Action Row
description: Wraps any row in a liquid glass card whose swipe actions are tinted glass bubbles. As the card slides they bud out of its edge, joined to it and to each other by liquid necks, and melt back in as it closes; the card lands in its detent at the speed you let go, a full swipe clicks in with a haptic as the edge bubble swallows the others and takes the bar, a destructive one carries the card out of the row, and a shared binding keeps one row open at a time.

contents.content: Row with swipe-to-reveal actions that works in a plain `VStack` or `ScrollView`, not only in `List`. The row is a liquid glass card and its actions are tinted glass bubbles. As the card slides they bud out of its edge and rest joined to it and to each other, so the open row is one liquid surface; closing, they melt back in.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The row is a liquid glass card (26pt continuous radius) and its actions are tinted glass bubbles with dark ink, `style.tileGap` (6pt) from the card and from each other. That gap sits inside the liquid merge distance, so an open row is one liquid surface: card and bubbles held together by necks. Pass light tints as `tint`; the house uses signal (`#FF0000`) for the one destructive or primary action and butter for a warning-like one such as snooze. On iOS 26 this is Liquid Glass; before that the same shapes draw as frosted Material, and under Reduce Transparency as solid fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Drags are only claimed when they start horizontally, so the enclosing `ScrollView` keeps vertical scrolling. The card stays under your finger. The row clips sideways, and the clip fades out over a short distance past each edge, so the glass's shadow is never cut by a hard line and a card slid past the edge slips away under the fade. A drag the system cancels (a scroll that takes over) lands the card in the nearest position and fires nothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Letting go keeps the card's speed: it settles into the open bubbles with a visible give, more the harder you flick, though never more than about a sixth of its travel past them, and a drag that closes comes home firmly. Tapping the card or a bubble, or opening and closing through the `open` binding, snaps it into place with a smaller give. Whether it opens or closes still depends on where the flick would carry it. Grabbing a card that is still landing never jumps: it finishes landing under your finger over the first tenth of a second.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Bubbles bud out of the card's edge: each is born just inside it, shrunk, where the two are one shape, and the reveal draws it out to its slot at the row's edge, pulling a neck as it goes. The edge bubble leads and each one further in follows a step behind, all driven by the card's place, so they never trail the finger and bud and melt exactly with the card when it springs. A bubble's color fills in as it clears the card and drains as it heads home; its glyph and label arrive once it is clear and blur away the moment the card heads home, so nothing ever sits on the card's glass. Opened past their slots, the bubbles stretch to fill the gap. A pressed bubble sinks a few points, glass and glyph together.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A full swipe (past 60% of the row width, and never less than two bubbles) clicks in like a detent: the other bubbles melt into the edge bubble as it swells across the whole bar, its glyph bounces once and a rigid impact fires as it arms, never as it lets go. Drag back before letting go and they bud out of it again. Past that line the card moves against rubber-band resistance; where the open bubbles reach further (several actions, or a narrow row), the resistance starts at them instead. Releasing runs that action. A destructive action (`role: .destructive`) carries the card on out of the row at the speed you let go, so removing the row in the handler reads as one motion. The edge bubble stays put and can't be tapped again while the card is out. If the row is still there 0.35s after the card is out (the handler asked first, or deletes later), the card comes back home and the bar melts into its edge. That pause outlasts a `List` delete or a default `withAnimation` removal; a removal slower than that shows the card returning as the row fades. Any other action brings the card home the same way. The first declared action sits at the screen edge, matching `.swipeActions`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass the same `open:` binding to every row in a list (with a unique `id:` per row) and only one row can be open at a time. Set the binding to `nil` to close all rows, or to a row's id to reveal its trailing actions (leading when there are none).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Swiping toward an edge with no actions gives with rubber-band resistance, never more than 60pt, and springs back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `background:` sets the card's glass: `nil` leaves it neutral, a color tints it. `.clear` suits a list that draws its own surface: there is no card, the content slides on its own, and with nothing to bud from the bubbles wait in their slots and are uncovered as the content slides off them.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`SwipeActionRow.Style`, also `SwipeActionRowStyle`): `tileInk`, `cornerRadius`, `tileWidth`, `tileGap`. `surface` is kept so existing code compiles but no longer draws anything: the card is glass. Set `cornerRadius` and `tileGap` to 0 for classic full-bleed list rows.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion keeps every state change and the arm haptic, but lands the card quickly with no overshoot or give, lets the bubbles wait in their slots and fade in with the reveal instead of budding, skips the arm bounce, and shades a pressed bubble instead of sinking it. All actions are exposed as VoiceOver custom actions on the row.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Need grouped activity with categorize, split and expanding detail? That is the Transaction Row screen in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Task Row
description: A task card with liquid glass chrome. Its check is a glass bubble, stamped in ink and popping as the check draws while the card flashes into a solid block, then settling to tinted glass as the row compacts; the priority sits on a tinted glass chip; a swipe-right buds a complete bubble out from under the card that completes with a strike-through; a swipe-left buds Snooze and Delete bubbles that part to rest apart; and a long-press lift reports reorder moves.

contents.content: Interactive task row for to-do lists, driven by a bound `Status`. The card stays a solid surface; its chrome is liquid glass. The check is a glass bubble, the priority a tinted glass chip, and the swipe actions are glass bubbles that bud out from under the card's edge as it slides.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Rows are soft cards (`style.surface`, 22pt radius) with liquid glass chrome. The check is a glass bubble: clear glass with a faint ring while open, the complete tint once done, the snooze tint with a moon while snoozed. Priority sits on a small tinted glass chip (HIGH signal, MED butter, LOW sky) with dark ink; due dates carry a clock glyph; a snoozed task gets a lilac glass Snoozed chip. On iOS 26 this is Liquid Glass; before that frosted Material, and under Reduce Transparency solid fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Completion is a sequence, not a toggle: the card flashes into the solid `tint` block (sage by default) while the check bubble is stamped in ink and pops with a `.success` haptic, the check draws in with a trimmed path, the strike-through grows across the title, then the row settles back and folds down compact with a slight give (smaller padding, type and check), the ink fading to show the tinted glass and the due label and priority folding away together. Setting `status` to `.completed` from outside runs the same sequence; rows that load already completed start settled. `.open` reverses it: the check and strike clear quickly, the bubble's tint drains and the row opens back up. Snoozing morphs the card in place: the check turns lilac with a moon, the due label swaps for the Snoozed chip and the priority folds away, staying hidden if the snoozed task is then completed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Swipe right to the 104pt detent to complete (or reopen a completed row). The card stays under the finger, and a round glass bubble buds out from under its leading edge: born there shrunk, drawn out to the middle of the gap by the swipe, its sage tint filling in as it clears the card. Its glyph stamps on with a rigid impact as the swipe arms, and past the detent the card moves against rubber-band resistance. Swipe left and Snooze (lilac) and Delete (signal) bubbles bud out the same way, only for the callbacks you pass: the outer one leads, the inner one follows a step behind, and they part through a liquid neck to rest apart. Pulled past them, the outer bubble stretches into the pull. Every bubble's label arrives once it is clear of the card and blurs away the moment the card heads home, and its tint drains as it goes back under.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On release the card keeps its speed: it settles into the bubbles with a visible give if the flick was heading there, more the harder you flick though never more than about a sixth of its travel past them. Let go on the right, completing or not, it comes home with a small give that stays short of the bubbles on the other side; closed from the left or flicked home fast, it comes home firmly. It springs back with a visible give from a side with nothing to reveal, and a tap on the card or a bubble snaps it home with a small give. Grab it again while it is still settling and it finishes landing under your finger. Bubbles and the check sink slightly when pressed, glass and glyph together.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Long-press (0.35s) to lift the row: once your finger has rested a moment the card presses into the table (a tap, scroll or swipe never dips it), then springs up to scale 1.03 with a soft impact while its shadow spreads a beat behind. Drag it vertically and `onMove` receives the number of row slots moved on release (negative is up). The card drops back into its slot at the speed you let go and its shadow gathers in after it, the card staying above its neighbors until both have landed, also when you let go without moving it. Animate your own array move in `onMove` if you want the other rows to slide. A touch the system cancels sets the card down without reporting a move. The gesture is only installed when `onMove` is set.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the swipe and the lift still track the finger, and every release lands on a short spring with no overshoot. The card doesn't press in or scale up (the shadow and haptics carry the lift), swipe bubbles wait at their places and fade in with the reveal instead of budding, the complete glyph brightens instead of stamping, the check doesn't pop, pressed bubbles and the check shade instead of sinking, labels fade instead of moving, and the completion steps crossfade at once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.disabled(true)` dims the row to 50% and turns off the swipe and lift.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`TaskRow.Style`): `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `ink`, `complete`, `snooze`, `delete`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `cornerRadius`. The tints color glass; `tint:` still overrides the complete color.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Stack rows with 8pt spacing on the ground. VoiceOver reads the row as one button with status, due date and priority, and exposes Complete/Reopen, Snooze, Delete and Move up/down as custom actions.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Need grouped-by-day activity with split and expanding detail? That is the Transaction Row screen in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Attachment Tray
description: A horizontal attachment strip for composers, support forms and listings: a liquid glass add tile opens the photo picker with the remaining limit, picks drop onto the strip as their own tiles carrying a glass status bubble with a live progress ring, and the remove badge buds out of it; the ring closes before the thumbnail, downsampled off the main thread, develops in place and the bubble melts into the badge, failures flood the bubble red as a retry, the remove badge cancels an in-flight load, duplicates and over-limit picks are caught, and the caller owns every attachment for upload.

contents.content: A strip of photo and video attachments with an add tile, per-item loading, retry, remove and a limit. Thumbnails are content; everything you press or read over them is liquid glass. A tile that is loading, failed or uploading carries a status bubble at its centre, joined to the remove badge in its corner. The badge buds out of that bubble when the tile drops onto the strip, and the bubble melts into the badge once the photo has developed. The caller owns the attachments. Picks from the built-in add tile are appended for you; anything else (a camera capture, a paste, a drop, a draft restored from disk, your own picker) is added by appending an `Attachment` to the binding, and the tray runs the same loading pipeline for it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Thumbnails are content; everything you press or read over them is liquid glass. The add tile is a glass tile with a solid red plus disc. A tile that is loading, failed or uploading carries a glass status bubble at its centre, joined by a liquid neck to the remove badge in its corner: the badge buds out of the bubble a beat after the tile drops onto the strip, and once the photo has developed the bubble melts up into the badge. On iOS 26 this is Liquid Glass; before that, a frosted material; under Reduce Transparency, solid fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: You own the attachments through a `@Binding [AttachmentTray.Attachment]`. Picks from the add tile are appended for you; the tray writes load progress, the thumbnail and the payload back by id, and removes an attachment when its badge is tapped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Anything else goes through the same pipeline by appending an attachment: `Attachment(image:)` for a camera capture or paste, `Attachment(data:)` for a drop or a saved draft, `Attachment(fileURL:)` for a file, `Attachment(item:)` for your own `PhotosPicker`, and `Attachment { progress in ... }` for your own download. For drops, add `.dropDestination(for: Data.self) { items, _ in attachments += items.map { .init(data: $0) }; return true }`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each tile goes loading, then loaded or failed. The ring in the status bubble spins until the source reports progress (an iCloud download, or your loader setting `totalUnitCount` and `completedUnitCount` on the `Progress` it is given), then fills smoothly with no overshoot. When a load finishes the attachment is loaded at once: the payload is set and VoiceOver reads Loaded. A ring that was showing progress fills and holds full for a beat (about 150 ms), then the photo develops under the bubble, settling from a slight zoom inside the tile without ever showing the tile's edge, while the bubble melts into the remove badge on a spring with no bounce. A video's duration badge, a glass capsule, rises in a beat later, and an upload dim you start right away appears with the photo. A failed load floods the bubble red, blurs the ring into a retry arrow and hangs "Retry" under it; tapping the tile, or calling `attachments[i].retry()`, drains the red and swaps the ring back as it loads again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Thumbnails are cut with ImageIO on a background task at the largest tile size times the screen scale, with orientation applied. The full-size image is never decoded, so a 48 MP photo costs a few hundred kilobytes, not a hundred megabytes. A text size change never triggers a reload.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Picked images keep their original bytes in `data` (HEIC stays HEIC, nothing is transcoded). `jpegData(maxPixelSize:compressionQuality:)` gives an upload-ready JPEG, downsampled, with location and other metadata removed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Videos (with `matching: .videos` or `.any(of: [.images, .videos])`) are copied to the temporary directory, never loaded into memory. `fileURL` points at the copy, the tile shows a poster frame and a duration badge, and `duration` is set. Delete the copy after upload if you need the space sooner than the system does.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Removing a tile cancels its load, including the photo library transfer. A load that finishes after its tile was removed, or after a newer attempt started, is dropped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The picker only allows the remaining count. Photos already in the tray (matched by library identifier, also within one pick) are skipped: the strip glides to their tile, which bumps once as it lands. Anything past the limit is left out with a warning haptic and one announcement. At the limit the add tile shows "6/6" and disables.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Set `uploadProgress` on an attachment to show your upload: the status bubble buds back out of the remove badge with the upload ring while the tile dims below 1, and once it reaches 1, a beat after the dim lifts, the bubble lands in the opposite corner as a sage check, whether or not you animate the write. Clearing `uploadProgress` melts the check back into the badge.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Empty, the add tile is wide and shows the title with "Up to 6". With attachments its glass narrows to a square with the count: the plus disc travels into place, the title clears out first and the count arrives after it, and later counts roll, never past the number they show. Picks drop onto the strip, settling from just above full size with a little give that dips just inside it (at most 5 pt past each edge, so larger tiles stay inside the strip), and every load starts at once. A first pick into an empty tray drops one after another in pick order, a beat apart (up to five beats, so a big pick never drags). Later picks, and tiles you append yourself, land together, and if the tray already had tiles the strip glides to the newest one. Removed tiles shrink away quickly with their glass and the rest close the gap. Tiles already in the tray when it appears (a restored draft) start with their badges in place.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Loaded tiles call `onSelect` when tapped, for example to open a full-screen viewer. Every tile has a context menu with Remove (and Retry when failed).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each tile is one element read as "Photo 2 of 4" with a value such as "Loading, 40%", "Couldn't load", "Uploading, 62%" or "Loaded", and Remove and Retry actions. The add tile reads its title and "3 remaining" or "Limit reached". Adds, skipped picks, removals and failures are announced once, and "All attachments loaded" when the last load finishes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact when picks land, a rigid impact on remove, a warning for skipped picks, an error when a load fails (one for a batch that fails together, such as when offline), a selection tick on retry. Presses play none.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type grows tiles up to 1.5 times `Style.tileSize`; text inside tiles stops growing at the same point so it never outgrows its tile. Right to left, the add tile leads from the right and badges sit top left; thumbnails are never mirrored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tiles with a tap action, the add tile and the remove badge sink slightly on press and spring back, centered so scrolling the strip is never disturbed; a pressed tile's glass sinks with it. A tile with nothing to do on tap (still loading, or loaded with no `onSelect`) stays still.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: tiles, the photo and the glass bubbles fade in place instead of budding and moving, picks arrive together, presses dim instead of sinking, a tile picked again flashes brighter instead of bumping, the add tile's plus disc and count crossfade instead of travelling and rolling, and the spinner is the system indicator. The progress ring still closes before the photo shows, and every haptic and announcement stays.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Horizontal inset: apply `.contentMargins(.horizontal, 20, for: .scrollContent)` to the tray so tiles line up with your content and still scroll to the screen edge.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the placeholder (`tile`), label and secondary colors, the badges' glass tint (`badge`, clear by default) and ink, the plus disc and retry tint (`signal`) and its ink, the uploaded check's tint, the corner radius, tile size and spacing. `.disabled(true)` dims the add tile, and the remove badges melt into their status bubbles (or thin away where there is none).

title: Link Preview
description: A rich card for any URL that holds its final size while a skeleton sweeps, then settles the page's image and title into place under a liquid glass host chip that is there from the first frame (riding over the picture on the large card), fetched once with LinkPresentation, shared by every card showing the same link and cached so scrolling never refetches, falling back to a quiet card with the address when a page cannot be read, opening on tap and offering Copy Link and Share on long press.

contents.content: A rich preview card for a URL: the page's image, title and host, fetched once and cached. The card is content; its one piece of chrome, the host, sits on a small liquid glass chip. It shows from the first frame (the host is known before the page is) and rides over the picture on the large card. Tapping opens `url` through the environment's `openURL`, so an app that shows links in its own browser routes it with `.environment(\.openURL, OpenURLAction { url in … })` like any other link.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `LinkPreview(url:)` fetches the page with LinkPresentation and shows its image, title and host. Pass `metadata:` to show your own (previews, tests, links your server already unfurled) with no request.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The card is content; its one piece of chrome, the host, sits on a small liquid glass chip: over the top leading corner of the picture on the large card, above the title on the compact one. The host is known before the page is, so the chip is there from the first frame, through the skeleton. A redirect blurs the final host in over the old one as the glass reshapes around it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Three states, one footprint. While loading, the card is a skeleton built from the real layout, so the large card keeps its exact size when the content arrives. The picture develops first, under its chip, fading in from just above full size and settling flat on the placeholder; the title starts on the same beat (nothing you read is held back) and rises a few points into the place its skeleton held, on a slightly softer spring with no bounce, so it settles just after and text never wobbles. A card that starts from the cache appears at once, with no animation. A page that cannot be read (offline, timeout, unknown host, a page with nothing in it) becomes the quiet address card: a link glyph, the host on its chip and the address, still tappable.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.compact` is a row with a square thumbnail, for chats and lists. `.large` puts a 1.91 : 1 image on top, capped at 280pt tall so a wide card crops instead of growing. Both take the width they are offered. A failed large card closes to the compact address card with no overshoot, so the feed below reflows once without bobbing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: No image falls back to the site icon on a quiet tile, then to the host's first letter on a solid block picked from the host, so a site keeps its color. A tiny "image" is treated as an icon rather than stretched.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Links that are not `http` or `https` never make a request: email, phone and message links show the address card with their own glyph and a chip such as "Email".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Redirects show the final host. Titles are trimmed with runs of whitespace collapsed, at most two lines (three at accessibility sizes). Long addresses truncate in the middle.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One cache for the whole app: at most 150 pages and about 48 MB of decoded images in an `NSCache`, emptied by the system under memory pressure. Cards showing the same URL share one fetch, a card that scrolls back into view starts from the cache with no skeleton, and a failure is remembered for 30 seconds so a failing link does not refetch on every scroll.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A card that disappears or changes its URL stops waiting at once; the fetch itself is cancelled when no card is waiting for it. A late result can never land on a card whose URL has changed. `timeout` (15 seconds) is enforced even while a connection is still being attempted.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each fetch uses its own `LPMetadataProvider`, created, started and cancelled on the main actor. Images are decoded and downsampled with ImageIO off the main actor and never kept at full size.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pressing sinks the card by a couple of points at each edge, from its center so it never fights a scroll, and it springs back on release. It stays opaque.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tap opens the link through the environment's `openURL`, so an app with its own browser routes it with `.environment(\.openURL, OpenURLAction { … })`. Long press shows Open Link, Copy Link and Share (with the title and image in the share sheet); copying plays a success haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: one element read as "Title, host" with the link trait, a Copy Link action, and "Loading preview" as its value while loading. Copying is announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: text scales, the thumbnail grows to 96pt, and at accessibility sizes the compact card stacks the text under the thumbnail at full width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the skeleton stops sweeping and breathes in place instead (a slow opacity pulse partway toward the highlight and back, on the same shared clock), so a loading card still shows it is working and its bones never fade into the card. The press darkens the card slightly (lightens it in dark mode) instead of sinking, and the picture and text fade in without scale or rise.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: All text is one weight, semibold; size sets the hierarchy. The chip is Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a frosted material before that, and a solid fill under Reduce Transparency.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the card, skeleton, highlight, title, secondary (the chip's text) and tile colors, the letter ink and the corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the card.

contents.heading: parameters

title: Photo Cropper
description: A crop step for profile photos, posts and listings that keeps the picked photo covering a frame of the chosen aspect at every zoom and offset, pinches around the fingers while it pans, rubber-bands past its limits and springs back with a red flash on the frame and a rigid tick at a zoom limit, morphs between circle, square, 4:5, 16:9 and the photo's own shape without losing the subject as a red liquid glass puck stretches along the aspect chips' glass track, turns a quarter at a time, fades in a rule-of-thirds grid under the finger, floats its zoom level over the photo on glass, and renders the crop off the main thread at the original's full resolution together with its pixel rect and rotation for cropping again on a server.

contents.content: A crop step for a picked photo: the photo under a frame of the chosen aspect, with pinch, pan, rotate and aspect chips. The photo is content; the controls around it are liquid glass. The aspect chips sit on one glass track, with a red puck under the selected one that stretches between picks. Rotate and Reset rest joined as one pair of tools, apart from Cancel and the red Choose capsule, and the zoom level floats over the photo on glass while you pinch. The photo always covers the frame. It can't be zoomed out or dragged so far that an empty edge stays in the frame: past a limit it resists and springs back on release. The framing is stored relative to the photo (zoom relative to the smallest scale that fills the frame, and the photo point at the frame's centre), so rotating, switching aspect and size changes keep the same subject in frame. Choose renders the crop from the original, off the main actor, and hands you a `Crop`. A drag that starts on the photo pans it; it never scrolls an enclosing scroll view or pulls a sheet down. ``swift @State private var photo: UIImage   // keep it in state, never create it in `body` PhotoCropper(image: photo, aspect: .circle, onCancel: { dismiss() }) { crop in avatar = crop.image dismiss() } ``

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The photo is content; the controls around it are liquid glass. The aspect chips sit on one glass track with a red puck under the selected chip. Rotate and Reset rest joined, one pair of tools for the crop, apart from Cancel and the red Choose capsule. The zoom level and any notice float over the photo on dark glass, since the well is dark in both appearances. On iOS 26 this is Liquid Glass; before that, a frosted material; under Reduce Transparency, solid fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Put it after a `PhotosPicker` (or the camera) in a `.fullScreenCover`, a pushed screen or a sheet. Keep the photo in state, for example `@State private var photo: UIImage?`, never created in `body`: a new image starts the cropper over.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The photo always covers the frame. Zoom is relative to the smallest scale that fills the frame (1 to 5, less for very small photos so a crop never drops below 32 pixels), and the framing is stored as that zoom plus the photo point at the frame's centre. Rotating, switching aspect, rotating the device and resizing all keep the same subject in frame.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pinch zooms about the fingers while they pan, both at once, and the photo stays exactly under them. Past the edges of the photo, or past 1x and the maximum zoom, it follows with a scroll view's resistance. Let go and it lands: a flick carries on at the photo's own speed into a short coast, a pull past an edge springs back from where the band left it, and a pinch past a limit comes back from rest. None of it bounces or runs past its stop: a coast stops where it's going, and a hard flick into an edge arrives fast and stops at the edge. Touch the photo before it has landed, or while a double tap, a key step or Reset is still zooming or moving it, and it stops where it is, under the finger, the way a scroll view does; a change of aspect or a turn always runs to its end. At a zoom limit the frame's edge and corner marks flash red for an instant with a rigid tick. Double-tap toggles between filling the frame and 2.5x about the tapped point.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A rule-of-thirds grid fades in the moment a finger touches the photo and out half a second after the last one lifts. The zoom level settles in above the frame on a glass capsule while pinching and lifts away with the grid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The aspect chips default to circle, square, 4:5, 16:9 and the photo's own shape; pass your own list (`[.square, .portrait, .ratio(3, 2)]`), retitle one with `.titled("Post")`, or pass a single aspect (or none) for a fixed frame. The red puck travels to the chip you pick as two tinted shapes, one landing with a little give and the other a beat behind, so it stretches along the track like a drop of liquid and gathers as it lands; the chip's picture turns solid ink on it. Meanwhile the frame and the photo morph to the new shape together without overshoot, so the photo never leaves part of the frame uncovered. `.circle` shows a round frame but the crop is square: clip it when you draw it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Rotate turns the photo a quarter to the left each tap; quick taps keep turning the same way. The turn never swings past its stop, and mid-turn the photo grows just enough that the frame's corners never leave it. `.original` turns with the photo.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Chips, Rotate, Reset, Cancel and Choose sink a little under the finger and spring back. Reset's label dims while there is nothing to reset.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Choose renders from the original, off the main actor, in the photo's own color space (Display P3 stays P3), upright, at up to `maxOutputDimension` (4096) on the longer side and never scaled up. `onCrop` gets a `Crop` with the `image`, the `rect` in pixels of the upright original and `quarterTurns` (to the left, applied after the rect), so a server can repeat the crop on the original, plus the `framing`. Choose spins until your `onCrop` returns, so you can await an upload there, then a check blurs in, and a beat later the label blurs back. The capsule holds its width throughout. If the cropper goes away mid-render the render is dropped; an `onCrop` that has started is never cut off.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `framing:` binds the aspect, zoom, centre and rotation instead of `aspect:`. Store `crop.framing` (it is `Codable`) and pass it back to reopen a crop where it was left, or drive the cropper from your own controls. Reset returns to the photo filling the starting aspect and is enabled only once something changed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: EXIF orientation is respected on screen and in the output. A photo that is much larger than the screen is shown from a copy cut once, off the main actor, so a 48 MP photo never decodes on the main thread; a quiet placeholder holds the frame meanwhile. A photo that can't be drawn shows "Couldn't open this photo" in the frame, and Choose and the puck drain to neutral glass. A failed render shows a short notice, rising in on glass at the bottom of the well, with an error haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A drag on the photo pans it: it never scrolls an enclosing scroll view or pulls a sheet down, because those pans wait for the cropper's own. Pinch and pan come from UIKit's recognizers, which report the fingers' moving centre.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a selection tick when the aspect changes, a light impact on rotate, a rigid tick at a zoom limit or an edge (once for a held key, not on every repeat), a soft tick on Reset, success when the crop is delivered, an error if rendering fails.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the photo is one adjustable element, "Crop area", with a value such as "2.5×, 4:5, Rotated left 90°". Swipe up and down to zoom, and use the Move up, down, left and right actions (a fifth of the frame each), Rotate left and Reset. Aspect chips are buttons with the selected trait ("4 to 5"), and rotations, resets and the finished crop are announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hardware keyboard: the arrow keys move and + and - zoom when the photo is focused, Return chooses, Escape cancels and Command-R rotates.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the photo lands, zooms and changes aspect on a short spring with no overshoot, a quarter turn crossfades to the turned photo and frame instead of swinging round, and the puck fades over to the chip you pick instead of travelling. The grid, the zoom level, the photo appearing and the red limit flash still fade, so you can follow what changed, and pressed buttons dim instead of sinking.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: chips and buttons scale (chips stop at the second accessibility size so the photo keeps its room). When the buttons no longer fit on one line, Choose moves to its own full-width row, and at the largest sizes Cancel does too; separate actions never come closer than the merge distance, so their glass never necks. Right to left mirrors the toolbar; the photo is never mirrored. All text is one weight, semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the toolbar ground, the photo's well (dark in both appearances so the photo, scrim and frame read the same), the scrim, the frame's edge, the red accent (Choose, the puck and the limit flash) and the ink on it, labels, the well's corner radius (`0` runs the photo edge to edge) and the frame inset. `control` and `selectedControl` are no longer used: the controls are neutral glass and the puck takes `accent`. `Messages` replaces any of the copy, such as `choose: "Use photo"`.

contents.content: Parameter

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Description

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `image`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The photo to crop, at full size, such as one loaded from a `PhotosPicker` item. Its orientation is respected. An on-screen copy is cut from it once, off the main actor; the crop is always rendered from this original. Keep it in state rather than creating it in `body`, or every update starts over.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `aspect`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The frame to start with. Defaults to `.square`.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `framing`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Bound framing, instead of `aspect`: the aspect, zoom, centre and rotation, updated as people adjust them. Set it to reopen a crop where it was left (`crop.framing` from an earlier result) or to drive the cropper from your own controls. While a finger is down it can briefly sit past the limits (the rubber band); it settles inside them on release.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `aspects`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The aspect chips under the photo, in order. Defaults to circle, square, 4:5, 16:9 and the photo's own shape. One aspect, or none, hides the chips for a fixed frame. An aspect that isn't listed is added at the front.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `maxOutputDimension`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The longest side of the rendered crop, in pixels. Defaults to 4096. Larger crops are scaled down to it; smaller ones keep the original's pixels and are never scaled up.

contents.heading: parameters

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The cropper's copy. Defaults are localizable through your String Catalog; replace any line, for example `choose` with "Use photo".

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `style`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Colors, the photo's well and the frame inset. Defaults to the SwiftPieces house palette, adapting to light and dark, with red for Choose, the selected aspect and the limit flash.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `onCancel`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Shows a Cancel button (and Escape on a hardware keyboard) that calls this. `nil` hides it.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `onCrop`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Called on the main actor with the rendered `Crop` when Choose is tapped (or Return is pressed). Choose keeps spinning until this returns, so you can await an upload here.

title: Photo Viewer
description: A full-screen photo surface with anchor-correct pinch zoom, momentum panning that gives a little at the bounds and rebounds, double-tap zoom about the tap, paging between images, and pinch-out or drag-down to dismiss with a fading scrim. A liquid glass close button and page counter float over the photos; while zoomed the counter floods with a light tint and rolls into a live zoom readout, and a single tap hides them.

contents.content: Photos-style viewer: page horizontally at rest, zoom and pan a page, pinch past the minimum or drag vertically to dismiss.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Zoom is anchored to the pinch start and to a double tap, so the content under the fingers stays put. Past `maxScale` the pinch meets resistance that stiffens toward a ceiling about 35% higher, with a rigid tick; releasing brings it back into range. A pinch released past `maxScale` comes back with no overshoot, so the photo never dips below its scale or opens its edge. A pinch released below `minScale` that doesn't dismiss rebounds with visible give when swelling past rest covers the photo's swing, as it does for any pinch that began at rest; one pinched out from a zoomed, off-center view comes back with no overshoot instead. A double tap or a VoiceOver action zooms in with a little give and zooms out with none. None of these swings the photo past an edge. Returning to `minScale` plays a soft tick.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pinch and pan follow the fingers directly, never animated. Past the scaled bounds a pan stiffens like a scroll view's edge. A released pan leaves at the finger's speed and coasts to `predictedEndTranslation`, clamped to the bounds, for longer the further it glides. An axis that runs into an edge keeps the finger's speed, carries on past the edge by a give that grows with the flick (under 80 pt), then rebounds; a pan that catches it there picks it up from inside the band instead of jumping.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At rest a page ignores horizontal drags so the paging `ScrollView` handles them; vertical drags and any drag during a pinch belong to the dismiss. Paging is disabled while zoomed or dismissing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Two dismiss paths: drag vertically past 140 pt (or flick past a projected 280 pt) and the page slides off along the release direction at the speed you threw it; pinch below 80% of `minScale` and release, and it shrinks away. Both fade the scrim with progress and call `onDismiss` when the animation is logically complete. A pull that doesn't commit slides home at the speed you let go and settles with some give, and the scrim and chrome come back with the photo rather than ahead of it. A drag that catches it on the way home picks it up where it is drawn, so it never jumps to the finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A pinch and a drag can end in either order: the page settles once both have let go, so it never strands below `minScale` or off center. A touch the system cancels (a call, Control Center) lets go the same way, without dismissing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion keeps every settle short with no overshoot or edge rebound, fades a committed dismiss where it is instead of flying or shrinking it, dims the close button on press instead of sinking it, and crossfades the counter instead of rolling its digits. Haptics and the scrim fade still mark each step. VoiceOver gets Zoom in, Reset zoom, and the escape gesture dismisses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Floating chrome in liquid glass, apart in its corners. A 44 pt glass close button (shown when `onDismiss` is set) fades the viewer out and calls `onDismiss`; a glass counter reads "2 / 3" at rest and, while zoomed, floods with a light tint as its digits roll into the zoom readout ("2.5×"). The chrome is the dark glass with paper ink in either appearance, since the viewer is a darkroom. A single tap hides or shows the chrome: it snaps into place with a slight give and leaves quickly, and fades as a dismiss drag progresses. The close button sinks on press; the counter's glass reshapes with a little give, into the readout or wider when the count gains a digit, while its digits roll without overshoot, so the count and zoom level never read past their value. With a single photo the readout drops in on its own once you zoom.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `style:` (`PhotoViewer.Style`) sets `scrim` (near-black #121212), `chromeInk`, `zoomFill` (the counter's tint while zoomed) and `zoomInk`, `showsCloseButton`, and `showsCounter`. `chromeFill` is no longer used: the chrome is liquid glass. `.bare` draws photos only. The chrome is Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a frosted material before that, and solid under Reduce Transparency; its text is semibold, and the photos you pass in keep their own type.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The example pages through flat color prints; a dismiss collapses the viewer and the example presents it again, so the preview only ever shows the viewer.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full gallery screen, see the Pro Gallery screen (`depth-gallery`).

contents.content: Scrim and chrome. `.standard` draws a near-black scrim and, in liquid glass over it, a close button when `onDismiss` is set and a counter that reads "2 / 5" at rest and the zoom level while zoomed.

title: Story Strip
description: A Stories-style segment strip with a built-in clock that advances segments on a duration, a long-press hold that freezes the strip and buds a liquid glass Paused badge down out of the bars (it melts back up into them on release), tap zones for back and forward that answer with a glass chevron bubble, and a manual progress mode when you own the timing.

contents.content: Segment strip plus the gesture surface of a story player. Pass `duration` to let it run itself, or leave it nil and drive `progress`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: With `duration` set the strip runs itself: a `TimelineView(.animation)` draws the fill and a task sleeps for the rest of the segment, then advances `current`. Pausing (a hold, or `isPaused`) records the pause time and shifts the segment start on resume, so the fill continues exactly where it stopped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Without `duration` the strip is stateless like before: you own `current` and `progress`, and steps animate with a short linear curve so 30 Hz updates read as continuous.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Holding anywhere on the surface for 200 ms pins the strip: the clock freezes on its frame and the bars dim at once with a soft tick. Releasing lifts the dim and resumes. A touch the system interrupts, such as an incoming call or Control Center, also lets go of the hold, so a story never stays paused. A shorter touch is a tap: the left 30% goes back (restarting the first segment when `duration` is set) and the rest advances, the moment the finger lifts.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Segment steps fill or empty the bars on a short spring that never overshoots, since the bars say where the story is. The running fill is a clock: it is drawn from the time every frame and never animated, so it stays exact and never bounces.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact when a hold engages, and one `.selection` tick for each move you ask for with a tap or a VoiceOver swipe that changes something, including restarting the first segment when `duration` is set. A move with nothing to change stays silent: forward after the story has finished, or back on the first segment when you drive `progress`, since there is no clock to restart. The clock's own advances and changes you make to `current` stay silent too, since a story can run for minutes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `fillsContainer` stretches the invisible surface over the whole story with the bars pinned to the top; set it to false to use only the bar row.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `onFinish` fires once when the last segment completes. VoiceOver reads "3 of 5", swipes up or down move between segments, and a custom action pauses or resumes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Holding buds a liquid glass "Paused" badge, tinted with the strip's `tint`, down out of the trailing end of the bars once the strip is pinned: it is born under the bars, springs out to its place, and its label sharpens just after. Let go and it rises back into the bars on a spring with no bounce, its label gone at once and its tint draining; the bars are not glass, so it thins away on the way and is gone by the time it gets there. A tap that moves back or forward flashes a glass chevron bubble in that zone, tinted the same way, which springs in with a little give, nudging in the direction of the move, and drifts on as it fades. Bars are 3 pt by default.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: With Reduce Motion the badge and the chevron fade in place instead of moving, and segment steps settle without overshoot. Under Reduce Transparency the glass draws solid. The dim, the haptics and the running fill are unchanged, so the strip still says when it is paused and where it is.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `style:` (`StoryStrip.Style`) sets `barHeight`, `spacing`, `trackOpacity`, `inset`, `showsPausedBadge`, `showsTapHints`, and `ink` (the glyph and text color on the glass, which is tinted with `tint`). `.minimal` restores the version 1 look. All text is one weight, semibold.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The example runs the strip in dark ink over solid color slides with one big idea each.
